films.name: The Assassin(s)
films.short_description: Undeterred by the intimidation of state agents, an intrepid detective, reporter and news editor join forces to uncover the truth about a shooting in this gripping procedural thriller.
films.description:
South Korea’s Liberation Day, 15 August 1974. Detective Cheol-gu leaves for work as part of the security team at the National Theater of Korea where president Park Chung-hee is due to make a national address. But the day descends into chaos when a shooting occurs.


After finding out that the crime scene tells a story contradicting official accounts, Cheol-gu, together with a young reporter and a newspaper editor, launches his own investigation to unearth the truth. Faced with the strong-arm tactics of a tyrannical government to silence dissent, the trio put their lives and careers on the line to pursue justice.


Though The Assassin(s) is a dramatised account of a historical event, the state-sponsored violence and communist bogeyman that mark this turbulent period of South Korean history are well documented. Hur Jin-ho’s sleek and accomplished procedural thriller offers a chilling look into a dictatorial regime where media freedom is suppressed and the law is twisted for political ends.

events.name: In Conversation With Shim Eun-kyung
events.description:
Join the conversation with Shim Eun-kyung, an acclaimed South Korean actress who has built a distinctive, boundary-crossing career in both South Korea and Japan.


Beginning her career at age nine as one of Korean television's most prominent child actors, Shim earned the Best Actress award at the Baeksang Arts Awards for her starring role in Miss Granny (2014). After expanding her work to Japan, she made history as the first Korean actor to win Best Actress at the Japan Academy Film Prize for The Journalist (2019). Her acclaimed performance in Two Seasons, Two Strangers (2025)—which won the Golden Leopard at the Locarno Film Festival—further earned her Best Actress at Japan's Kinema Junpo Best Ten Awards.


In this exclusive dialogue session, Shim will share insights into her evolution as a performer working across borders and languages, and how she continues to forge a singular path as a generation-defining actress.


Moderated by: TBC

Conducted in Korean with English interpretation
events.short_description: Join acclaimed South Korean actress Shim Eun-kyung as she discusses her evolution from prominent child star to history-making, award-winning international lead across both Korean and Japanese cinema in this exclusive dialogue session.

films.name: Cageman
films.short_description: A colourful cast of working-class Hong Kongers resists eviction from their bedspace apartments in this humanistic reflection of pre-1997 Hong Kong.
films.description:
In Hong Kong’s squalid tenements, low-income ‘cagemen’ live in bunk beds separated by chicken wire, forming an intimate camaraderie within their cramped shared space. When news of a planned eviction arrives, the media, police, lawyers and politicians, each with their own agendas, descend upon the community. The residents must decide whether to relent or resist.


Inspired by a fatal fire in a cage home in 1990, Jacob Cheung casts a sympathetic eye on the plight of those most impacted by the city’s corrupt bureaucracy and capitalism, while recognising their humour and resilience.


Naturalistic performances and authentic dialogue from an ensemble cast breathe life into the endearing, good-natured characters. With long takes that highlight the claustrophobia and clamour of the environs, Cageman is an immersive portrayal of cage homes. It is a humanistic work that celebrates communal spirit and agency while gently indicting opportunistic and hypocritical authority figures.

events.description: This screening includes a Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: Baby Jackfruit Baby Guava
films.short_description: With humour and heart, a queer filmmaker turns the camera on his family, revealing how love, identity and belonging are reshaped in contemporary Vietnam.
films.description:
Long-buried tensions, unspoken identities and unresolved love have shaped filmmaker Nông Nhật Quang’s family for years. When a new chapter in his older sister Mai's life begins, the fragile balance that has held the family together starts to shift, prompting Quang to turn the camera towards his kin.


Believing that filmmaking can open conversations where words have failed, Quang retraces his changing bond with Mai, reflects on his own journey as a gay son, and gently navigates the fraught relationship between his mother and sister. Intimate and deeply compassionate, Baby Jackfruit Baby Guava invites audiences into a Vietnamese family who are learning to give voice to years of silence.


The film assembles family photographs, diaries, phone recordings and home videos into a vibrant first-person documentary where memories collide with the present. With candid observation, sharp humour and queer exuberance, Nông embraces the camera not as a tool of objectivity but as a way of speaking to his loved ones. An emerging voice in Vietnamese queer cinema, he captures a generation negotiating greater LGBTQ+ visibility in a society where the hardest conversations still begin at home.

events.name: In Conversation With Aamir Khan
events.description:
The Festival is proud to present an exclusive conversation with this year’s SGIFF Screen Icon Award recipient, Aamir Khan – one of Indian cinema’s most influential and acclaimed actors, directors, and producers.


Renowned for his dedication to craft and socially conscious storytelling, Khan will reflect on his stellar career in cinema spanning four decades. Possessing one of the most commercially impactful and critically acclaimed filmographies in Indian cinema history, he has reshaped global perceptions of Indian cinema—from founding Aamir Khan Productions to steering Oscar-nominated epics and record-breaking blockbusters.


Khan has received four National Film Awards and nine Filmfare Awards in his career and made his directorial debut with the critically acclaimed Taare Zameen Par (2007). He has also produced and starred in the epic Lagaan (2001), which earned an Academy Award nomination.


Don’t miss this rare opportunity to gain insights from a global screen icon whose performances, work ethic and dedication to cinema continue to enthrall fans all over the world.


Moderated by: Rishi Budhrani, Host and Actor

Conducted in English
events.short_description: Join SGIFF Screen Icon Award recipient Aamir Khan as he reflects on a four-decade filmmaking career of groundbreaking Indian cinema classics. In this exclusive dialogue, the Indian cinema icon will share rare insights into his journey as a pioneer behind and in front of the camera.

films.name: Mayilaa
films.short_description: In this exuberant spin on the road movie, a rural mother-daughter pair become unlikely salespeople as they navigate inequalities and faith.
films.description:
After leaving her abusive husband, Mayilaa makes a meagre living while raising her daughter, who suffers from constipation. She banks on her pluck along with a peculiar, fiercely devoted connection to the village goddess whose name she shares. But when Mayilaa loses her job and a religious duty looms, she must hit the road and leave her village in rural Tamil Nadu to sell straw mats, with her daughter in tow.


On a cranky moped, knocking on door after door, she often runs up against chauvinism or classism. But the world beyond her village offers its own curiosities too. Mayilaa’s travels often bring her into the orbits of women entirely unlike her, who lovingly extend solidarity or remain coolly indifferent, all to her wonder.


From its nonprofessional cast to the unassumingly infectious rhythm, Mayilaa is a debut that brims with confidence. Its neorealist observation and surrealist sequences suture multitudes within the material and spiritual lives of women in rural India. Delivering a lively vision of feminist freedom with a dose of scatological humour, Mayilaa paints a woman’s defiance with care and empathy.

events.name: In Conversation With Peter Chan
events.description:
Join the conversation with Peter Ho-sun Chan, a leading figure in contemporary Chinese-language cinema and the first director to have won three major directing awards at the Hong Kong Film Awards, Golden Horse Awards, and Golden Rooster Awards.


Emerging during Hong Kong's golden age of cinema, Chan co-founded United Filmmakers Organization (UFO) in 1991, shaping iconic urban melodramas like Comrades, Almost a Love Story (1996). His vision later expanded internationally with DreamWorks' The Love Letter (1999) and pan-Asian production company Applause Pictures. By directing acclaimed blockbusters like Perhaps Love (2005), The Warlords (2007) and Wu Xia (2011), Chan seamlessly blends commercial appeal, genre storytelling, and artistic vision.


In this exclusive dialogue session, Chan will share insights into his four-decade cinematic legacy, and how he continues to be an advocate for the Chinese-language film industry and broader pan-Asian collaborations.


Moderated by: TBC

Conducted in English
events.short_description: Join master filmmaker Peter Chan for an exclusive dialogue on his four-decade cinematic legacy, as he shares insights on blending commercial success with artistic vision, and the future of Chinese-language and pan-Asian cinema.

events.name: The Uncharted Potential of Location-Based VR
events.description:
A renowned group of French location-based virtual reality companies come together to discuss their productions and explore the multidimensional business and public engagement applications of this medium.


Location-Based Virtual Reality (LBVR) refers to an immersive form of VR in which virtual environments are experienced within specially designed physical settings. While conventional VR generally involves one user at a time, LBVR is designed for several participants to experience the same interactive virtual environment simultaneously. Participants can therefore move together in a physical space while interacting within a shared virtual world.


This programme is supported by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs (France) and the Institut français.


Speakers

Mathieu Barbier, Studio Director, Atlas V

Eric Barbedor, Author and Creative-Technologist, Backlight

Richard Turco, Executive Director, Innerspace

Chloe Jarry, CEO, Lucid Realities

Emanuela Righi, Producer, Novaya

Voyelle Acker, Co-founder and Head of Content and Distribution, Small Creative


Moderator

events.name: Voooooo---Peeeeee---
events.description:
Voooooo---Peeeeee--- is a multisensory XR experience where a woman discovers her body has become hollow after being reconstructed as data. Wind leaks from within, and a strange creature settles in the void, breathing in rhythms of expansion and collapse. Her monologue drifts between memories of loss, data clouds beneath the sea, and endlessly replicated virtual worlds. Through VR cinema and a pneumatic wearable interface, audiences physically experience this expanding virtual volume as pressure and breath, entering a space where bodily presence and technological space overwrite one another.

Ubac Studio is a Seoul-based media artist duo composed of Hyeunjoo Woo and Jiyun Park. Working primarily with XR-based interactive installations, they explore moments when technology’s construction of the world collides with individual sensory experience. Their works have been presented at Cannes Immersive and Venice Immersive, and received the Festivals Connexion Award at Annecy 2026.

events.name: French Location-Based VR
events.description:
Experience award-winning immersive productions by a renowned group of French location-based virtual reality companies.

While conventional VR generally involves one user at a time, LBVR is designed for several participants to experience the same interactive virtual environment simultaneously. This programme is supported by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs (France) and the Institut français.


Artists

Atlas V

Atlas V is a global leader in immersive entertainment, driven by storytelling & innovation.

Since 2016, Atlas V has been pushing the boundaries of virtual reality, creating award-winning immersive experiences, video games, and exhibitions with proven critical and commercial success worldwide.

Building on its strong narrative DNA, Atlas V is now expanding into multiplayer location-based entertainment and accessible casual gaming, bringing immersive experiences to broader audiences and new social contexts.

From premium narrative worlds to shared, competitive, and playful experiences, the company bridges high-end creative ambition with scalable, audience-driven formats. We craft emotionally powerful, visually striking worlds that connect cutting-edge technology with a strong creative vision—designed to be experienced together, across platforms and territories.


Backlight

BackLight is an XR production studio based in Paris and founded in 2008. A pioneer in XR in the fields of entertainment and cultural experiences, the studio is renowned for its tailor-made productions and its alliance of creative innovation and technical ambition.

BackLight’s productions have been presented in prestigious venues across France, including the Théâtre National de Chaillot, Palais Garnier, La Seine Musicale, Le Palace Paris, Maison Hennessy, and the Musée d’Orsay, and internationally at renowned institutions such as Teatros del Canal (Madrid), the Barbican Centre (London), the LAFAYETTE Cultural Arts Center (Shanghai), and the Xinjiang Museum (China).

The studio’s creations have been officially selected by leading international festivals and showcases worldwide and have received numerous distinctions, including the Venice Immersive Grand Prize (Lion Award) at the Venice International Film Festival for Le Bal de Paris.


Innerspace

Founded in 2014 by artists Balthazar Auxietre and Hayoun Kwon, Innerspace has emerged as one of the leading creative studios in the virtual reality industry, both in France and internationally. Driven by a passion for exploring the artistic potential of immersive technologies, the studio combines innovation and creativity with a delicate balance between storytelling and interactivity. From location-based immersive installations to online video games, Innerspace’s projects have captivated audiences and earned acclaim at major festivals and from critics worldwide. The studio’s ambition is to continue pushing the boundaries of XR, blending entertainment with artistic excellence to engage ever-larger audiences and deliver experiences that leave a lasting impact.


Lucid Realities

Lucid Realities is an immersive and interactive production based in Paris, co-founded by Chloé Jarry and François Bertrand. It has also a distribution branch through its affiliate company Unframed Collection that powers the first distribution platform for VR contents dedicated to cultural venues (www.unframed-collection.com).

The projects powered by Lucid Realities are designed to foreshadow the future of the XR industry and innovate ways to

produce and distribute XR experiences. For us, XR is more than technology: it’s an opportunity to create unprecedented emotional ways to connect people with edutainment contents.


Novaya

Novaya is a Paris-based production company dedicated to immersive works, founded in 2021. It creates new forms of immersive storytelling and develops the technologies that bring them to life. Novaya produced NOIRE — winner of Best Immersive Work at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival, now touring more than twenty venues across fifteen countries — and leads FABRIC, a France 2030 laureate: a unique hybrid capture stage being built at the Studios de Bry-sur-Marne with IRCAM and INRIA, designed to capture live performance in volume, movement and sound, and make it possible to experience it anywhere, across time and space.


Small Creative

Small Creative is a French immersive studio founded in Paris, specializing in the design, production and distribution of premium collective and free roaming VR experiences, in which groups of up to 15 people explore shared virtual worlds together, untethered and in complete freedom of movement. From the wreck of the Titanic to the arenas of ancient Rome, from the gardens of Versailles to the summit of Everest, Small Creative transforms iconic stories and places into powerful, shared emotional journeys. The company produces up to six new experiences per year and has already deployed its work in more than 50 cities across Europe, Americas, Asia and the Middle East, working with cultural institutions, location-based entertainment operators and private venue partners.

films.name: All of a Sudden
films.short_description: Enveloped in care and tenderness, the conversations between a Paris nursing home director and a dying Japanese playwright become a space for gradual transformation.
films.description:
Marie-Lou runs a nursing home outside Paris, struggling against a system that treats care as a cost to be minimised. When she encounters Mari, a Japanese playwright who is terminally ill, the two begin a series of conversations that bridge the cultural, personal and emotional distances between them. Each exchange, marked by shared curiosity and admiration, expands to hold these differences.


All of a Sudden is built around long, unhurried dialogue, where conversations become a transformative space. As it moves between art, performance and companionship, the film explores a radical idea of care: attention, listening and presence as acts of resistance in systems that prize efficiency over genuine connection.

films.name: Rehearsals for a Revolution
films.short_description: Through five generations of personal stories, this documentary reveals how memories of resistance survive beyond political upheavals. A poetic portrait of Iran’s ongoing struggle, it explores storytelling and everyday acts of defiance as quiet forms of revolution.
films.description:
Through five intimate portraits, Pegah Ahangarani revisits 50 years of Iran’s history, revealing how political upheavals reverberate across generations. Beginning with her father’s journey from revolutionary idealism to disillusionment, the film follows her uncle’s hopes for reform, her teacher’s encounter with repression, Ahangarani’s political awakening during the 2009 Green Movement, and the new possibilities embodied by her young daughter.


The film blends family archives, photographs, recordings and historical footage into a poetic documentary essay. Through recollection and reassembling fragments of the past, Ahangarani explores storytelling, remembrance and artistic expression as quieter forms of revolution.

events.name: Artist Spotlight: Shaheer Tarar + Hsu Che-Yu and Chen Wan-Yin
events.description:
In this two-part session, hear from artist Shaheer Tarar, followed by Hsu Che-Yu and Chen Wan-Yin on their creative practices which reinvent filmmaking pproaches through innovative uses of tools, mixed media, and software. The Compression Zone by Shaheer Tarar and Corporeal Forms: Four Stories by Hsu Che-Yu and Chen Wan-Yin are presented under the Undercurrent section.


Speakers

Shaheer Tarar is a media artist and geographer based in London. He pursues socio-political stories buried in time, space, sediment, and code, examining artifacts that shape how the world is seen and governed. His recent work comprises a series of net-art projects and experimental video games that trace how digital images are haunted by the infrastructures that produce them, and how those images generate competing worldviews. He has exhibited this work at transmediale (Berlin), The Photographers’ Gallery (London), Akademie Schloss Solitude (Stuttgart), Peckham Digital (London), and InterAccess (Toronto). He is currently a Lecturer in the Graphic Communication Design programme at Central Saint Martins.


Hsu Che-Yu and Chen Wan-Yin have been collaborating since 2014. Their collaborative works have been presented primarily as solo exhibitions at Kunstverein in Hamburg (2026), Center of Contemporary Art – Tbilisi (2025), Hong Foundation (Taipei, 2025), Vanguard Gallery (Shanghai, 2025, 2020, 2016), ARGOS Centre for Audiovisual Arts (Brussels, 2024), ILHAM Gallery (Kuala Lumpur, 2024), Fundació Joan Miró (Barcelona, 2023), Centre d’Art Contemporain Genève (2023), MOCA Taipei (2023), Vernacular Institute (Mexico City, 2023), Kuandu Museum of Fine Arts (Taipei, 2023), Liang Gallery (Taipei, 2022), and the Taipei Fine Arts Museum (2015). Their work has also been included in group exhibitions at Kunstenfestivaldesarts (Brussels, 2024), Theater der Welt (Frankfurt, 2023), Bienal de São Paulo (2021), Seoul Mediacity Biennale (2021), VIDEONALE.18 (Bonn, 2021), the Shanghai Biennale (2018), and the Asian Art Biennial (Taichung, 2017), as well as in film festivals including the International Film Festival Rotterdam (IFFR) (2023, 2022, 2020, 2018) and the New York Film Festival (NYFF) (2020).

events.name: Trust by Design: AI, Ethics & Creative Work
events.description:
New tools come with terms and conditions—and creative workers would quite like a hand in writing them. Bringing together law, industry and research, this panel explores how AI is reshaping authorship, consent, ownership and working lives—the questions no software update will settle. With Singapore and Asia in focus, discover what meaningful protection, fair opportunity and real accountability could look like in practice, and how creators can have a stronger voice in the decisions that shape their work.


Speakers

Jessie Tan, Managing Partner; Shin Associates

Jessie Tan is Managing Partner of Shin Associates and one of Malaysia’s leading TMT and entertainment lawyers. Working at the intersection of creativity, technology and commerce, she advises studios, producers, platforms and rights holders on bringing stories to screen, protecting creative rights and navigating a rapidly evolving digital landscape.


Dixon Soh, Director, Head of Intellectual Property and Intangible Assets Practice, CHP Law LLC

Dixon Soh sees IP not as a legal instrument but as the architecture of future value. His work spans the creative economy, technology, and beyond. He has advised fast-growing companies across gaming, e-commerce, media tech, and artificial intelligence, and has structured IP strategies for businesses at every stage, from startups to established enterprises reinventing themselves through their intangible assets.


Pei-Sze Chow, Assistant Professor of Digital Culture and New Media; Wee Kim Wee School of Communication and Information, NTU

Pei-Sze Chow is a critical media scholar researching how AI is transforming creative work in the cultural and creative industries. She speaks regularly at international academic and industry events on creative labour and AI governance in the cultural sector. She co-founded the Asian Media Industries Research Network and is advisor to the Women* in AI, Humanities, and Social Sciences initiative.


Moderator

Wonsun Shin, Curator of Parallax

Wonsun Shin is a freelance consultant with extensive experience in co-production projects, festival strategies, and remake rights acquisitions. She began her career at CJ Entertainment, collaborating with Paramount Pictures and DreamWorks for film marketing. As Director of Film Festival Strategies, she built strong relationships with major festivals, a practice she continues today. Wonsun has been a jury and selection committee member for prestigious project markets and industry programs such as NAFF BIFAN, NFDC Film Bazaar Goa, and Fantastic 7 at Cannes. In 2024, she participated in the Cannes Investors Circle selection committee at Marché du Film and the first round of project selections for the Hubert Bals Fund. Her talent for identifying emerging voices and cultivating global connections has been a defining feature of her professional journey.

films.name: Lagaan: Once Upon a Time in India
films.short_description: Set during the British Raj, the people of a small, drought-stricken village in Central India wager on a game of cricket against their ruthless colonial rulers in order to avoid paying high taxes.
films.description:
In the town of Champaner in Central India, Bhuvan, a farmer, hastily assembles eleven players to form a cricket team before the season commences. His unorthodox recruitment process soon puts together a ragtag team, with the commanding officer’s sister as their coach who teaches them the game rules. Their hope is to beat the British team in order to avoid paying the high taxes (lagaan) levied on them. But before the first ball’s bowl, suspicion and sabotage threaten to unravel Bhuvan’s team.


Ashutosh Gowariker stages the three-day match as a sweeping ensemble piece, following each player’s redemption through interpersonal strife. These range from rekindled rivalries to caste prejudice which threaten to splinter the team. By the end of the games, individual wins are celebrated as communal triumph in this classic sports epic.

films.name: The Compression Zone
films.short_description: A video game descends into a pixel dungeon where demons demand a sacrifice for your data
films.description:
Playing alongside the game’s protagonist, we descend into a techno-pastel dungeon called The Compression Zone, where data demons offer to act as our messengers but demand something in return: a Faustian pact for our times. Homebrewed on the Unity engine and updated at every performance, Shaheer’s video game shifts our focus to the tools of perception in our digitally mediated realities. It unpacks how the algorithmic logics of data infrastructure shape what we see: data is packaged and compiled, deployed across corners of the globe, stretching over land and coursing through undersea fibre-optic lines—leaving imprints on the very environments they render on our screens.


Drawn partly from his move from Lahore to Canada during his growing-up years, the video-game lecture traces the expansion of cartographic imagination precipitated by the early internet. At the same time, it explores how the convenience of instant knowledge rests on compression algorithms that make a value judgement about what counts as ‘loss’ in the process.

films.name: The Diary of a Chambermaid
films.short_description: Gianina leaves behind her daughter in Romania to cook, clean and care for a family in France. At night, she rehearses a scandalous play about domestic servants—a vulgar, exaggerated version of the exploitation she quietly endures.
films.description:
Gianina, a young woman from rural Romania, works as a housekeeper, cook and nanny for a bourgeois family in France. She navigates their genial condescension and cares for their son, while trying to maintain a bond with her own daughter through video calls. At night, she rehearses a play based on Octave Mirbeau's The Diary of a Chambermaid, a salacious novel from 1900 that skewers upper-class hypocrisy.


Radu Jude’s metafictional take on domestic servitude confronts the insidious patterns of contemporary exploitation and the limits of performative empathy. This story of migrant labour and maternal sacrifice finds the prolific satirist at his most heartfelt, without losing any of his acerbic wit.

films.name: September Afternoon
films.short_description: As summertime ends, a couple, their young child and an acquaintance visit the beach, but are beset by strong winds and a slowly encroaching calamity. This strange film uses colour, mise-en-scène and sound design to suggest another way of experiencing the emptiness and dread of time.
films.description:
As summer comes to a close, a couple and their young child prepare to visit the beach. Accompanied by their acquaintance, they make their way to the seaside. However, powerful winds stymie their attempts to walk, play and rest, as hints of a cataclysm gradually materialise. Bracketed by a 1985 ice-cream commercial and a key moment from a 1968 Philippe Garrel film, September Afternoon languorously unfolds, punctuated by uncanny mise-en-scène.


As time ticks on, seemingly banal gestures of leisure and enjoyment seem to take on altered significance. Interminable strains of pop music, combined with the diegetic roar of wind and waves, take the place of dialogue. Schmidt uses colour, composition, editing and sound design in this unforgettable film to convey a feeling of disassociation, as if we are suspended in the moment of a great, nameless transition.

films.name: You Dreamt You Saw Yourself But Couldn’t See Your Face
films.short_description: Fluid reflections in water and the haunting sound of wind become metaphors for loss, mourning and the passage of time in this personal work featuring three generations of a family.
films.description:
The flow of water and sound of wind become metaphors for mourning and the passage of time in this tender work about intergenerational relationships. A memorial service for a loved one that took place at two rivers inspired Seno to depict still and moving surfaces of water by layering her 16mm film and digital footage.


As leaves and twigs break through rippled reflections of the sky and landscape, distant figures from the past seem to appear from beneath the water, alongside images of family members crouched at the riverbank. The sound of rushing wind haunts the soundtrack, bracketed by a whistled tune from the past, and a whispered voice speaking about what is to come.

films.name: Tangles
films.short_description: A young graphic artist returns home to care for her mother who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer’s. In the process, she finds grief, comedy and first love tangled together in a household relearning how to love a person they thought they knew.
films.description:
Sarah puts her exciting life as an activist and artist in 90s San Francisco on hold and returns to her small, conservative hometown after her mother’s Alzheimer’s diagnosis. While her father struggles with his own grief, Sarah’s caregiving duty affects every part of her life, including her romantic relationship. Despite the heartrending effects of Alzheimer’s, the film imbues her mother with a personality beyond the disease: feisty, funny, with flashes of her old self.


Tangles adapts Sarah Leavitt’s memoir for the screen without sanding down its unique traits as a graphic novel. Hand-drawn, black-and-white animation reimagines the source visual language, using sound design and movement to give the story a life distinctly its own, staying faithful to both mediums.

Experience award-winning immersive productions by a renowned group of French location-based virtual reality companies.


Location-Based Virtual Reality (LBVR) refers to an immersive form of VR in which virtual environments are experienced within specially designed physical settings. While conventional VR generally involves one user at a time, LBVR is designed for several participants to experience the same interactive virtual environment simultaneously. Participants can therefore move together in a physical space while interacting within a shared virtual world.


This programme is supported by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs (France) and the Institut français.


Artists

Atlas V

Atlas V is a global leader in immersive entertainment, driven by storytelling & innovation.

Since 2016, Atlas V has been pushing the boundaries of virtual reality, creating award-winning immersive experiences, video games, and exhibitions with proven critical and commercial success worldwide.

Building on its strong narrative DNA, Atlas V is now expanding into multiplayer location-based entertainment and accessible casual gaming, bringing immersive experiences to broader audiences and new social contexts.

From premium narrative worlds to shared, competitive, and playful experiences, the company bridges high-end creative ambition with scalable, audience-driven formats. We craft emotionally powerful, visually striking worlds that connect cutting-edge technology with a strong creative vision—designed to be experienced together, across platforms and territories.


Backlight

BackLight is an XR production studio based in Paris and founded in 2008. A pioneer in XR in the fields of entertainment and cultural experiences, the studio is renowned for its tailor-made productions and its alliance of creative innovation and technical ambition.

BackLight’s productions have been presented in prestigious venues across France, including the Théâtre National de Chaillot, Palais Garnier, La Seine Musicale, Le Palace Paris, Maison Hennessy, and the Musée d’Orsay, and internationally at renowned institutions such as Teatros del Canal (Madrid), the Barbican Centre (London), the LAFAYETTE Cultural Arts Center (Shanghai), and the Xinjiang Museum (China).

The studio’s creations have been officially selected by leading international festivals and showcases worldwide and have received numerous distinctions, including the Venice Immersive Grand Prize (Lion Award) at the Venice International Film Festival for Le Bal de Paris.


Innerspace

Founded in 2014 by artists Balthazar Auxietre and Hayoun Kwon, Innerspace has emerged as one of the leading creative studios in the virtual reality industry, both in France and internationally. Driven by a passion for exploring the artistic potential of immersive technologies, the studio combines innovation and creativity with a delicate balance between storytelling and interactivity. From location-based immersive installations to online video games, Innerspace’s projects have captivated audiences and earned acclaim at major festivals and from critics worldwide. The studio’s ambition is to continue pushing the boundaries of XR, blending entertainment with artistic excellence to engage ever-larger audiences and deliver experiences that leave a lasting impact.


Lucid Realities

Lucid Realities is an immersive and interactive production based in Paris, co-founded by Chloé Jarry and François Bertrand. It has also a distribution branch through its affiliate company Unframed Collection that powers the first distribution platform for VR contents dedicated to cultural venues (www.unframed-collection.com).

The projects powered by Lucid Realities are designed to foreshadow the future of the XR industry and innovate ways to

produce and distribute XR experiences. For us, XR is more than technology: it’s an opportunity to create unprecedented emotional ways to connect people with edutainment contents.


Novaya

Novaya is a Paris-based production company dedicated to immersive works, founded in 2021. It creates new forms of immersive storytelling and develops the technologies that bring them to life. Novaya produced NOIRE — winner of Best Immersive Work at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival, now touring more than twenty venues across fifteen countries — and leads FABRIC, a France 2030 laureate: a unique hybrid capture stage being built at the Studios de Bry-sur-Marne with IRCAM and INRIA, designed to capture live performance in volume, movement and sound, and make it possible to experience it anywhere, across time and space.


Small Creative

Small Creative is a French immersive studio founded in Paris, specializing in the design, production and distribution of premium collective and free roaming VR experiences, in which groups of up to 15 people explore shared virtual worlds together, untethered and in complete freedom of movement. From the wreck of the Titanic to the arenas of ancient Rome, from the gardens of Versailles to the summit of Everest, Small Creative transforms iconic stories and places into powerful, shared emotional journeys. The company produces up to six new experiences per year and has already deployed its work in more than 50 cities across Europe, Americas, Asia and the Middle East, working with cultural institutions, location-based entertainment operators and private venue partners.

films.name: Minotaur
films.short_description: As Russia descends into war, an influential businessowner in a small town decides whose lives are disposable. His betrayals pile up, exposing the moral and political corruption that insulates the powerful while the world burns.
films.description:
As Russia descends into war, Gleb, an influential businessowner in a small town, is asked to draw up a list of able-bodied staff he can spare for the draft. Meanwhile, his marriage has gone stale, and he suspects his wife is having an affair. With personal and professional pressures mounting, Gleb takes dramatic steps to protect his interests.


Exiled director Andrey Zvyagintsev transposes Claude Chabrol’s La Femme Infidèle onto wartime Russia, turning the erotic thriller into an indictment of the ruling class. Austere, widescreen compositions lend a disquieting elegance to this moral reckoning, in which the rot of society begins at home and human sacrifice is cruelly exacted to feed continual violence.

films.name: Amores Perros
films.short_description: A fatal car crash links three strangers’ lives: a young man entering the world of dogfighting, a supermodel whose life is derailed after the accident, and an ex-guerrilla trying to reconcile with his past.
films.description:
The lives of three strangers from different segments of society intertwine after a tragic car crash in Mexico city: a young man who enters the feral world of dogfighting to make money in order to run away with his brother’s wife. A supermodel whose life has been derailed by the crash and is struggling to find her dog that has disappeared into her apartment floorboard. And an aging hitman who lives with a pack of stray dogs and is desperate to reconnect with his estranged daughter.


Iñárritu’s unflinching feature debut, like a rabid mongrel, latches onto these characters as they seek reprieve from their respective circumstances. Amid the messy cycles of violence in a relentlessly harsh city marked by segregation, they struggle to find human connection.

events.name: Six Months in a Pink and Blue Building

films.name: Six Months in a Pink and Blue Building
films.short_description: In this coming-of-age docufiction, an eleven-year-old reckons with his queer identity while coping with his father’s HIV diagnosis amid the moral panic of the 1990s AIDS epidemic.
films.description:
Eleven-year-old Bruno celebrates his birthday with an exuberant drag party with family and friends. But two momentous events puncture the merriment: Bruno realises he has a crush on his best friend, and his father is diagnosed with HIV. As Bruno grapples with his queer identity amid the moral panic of the 1990s AIDS epidemic, the impending familial tragedy weighs heavily. Despite the crushing news, his family tries to maintain a buoyant mood—but how long can that last?


Loosely based on the director’s life, this affecting docufiction dramatises his emotional memory of a turning point in his childhood while present-day interviews add another layer of subjectivity. The nostalgic 16mm cinematography filled with candy-coloured hues brings to life a coming-of-age story that brims with tenderness.

events.name: In Conversation With Hirokazu Koreeda
events.description:
The Festival is proud to present an exclusive conversation with this year’s SGIFF Cinema Honorary Award recipient, Hirokazu Koreeda – a leading figure in Japanese cinema renowned for his deeply humanist works and naturalistic, observational storytelling.


Koreeda will reflect on an acclaimed filmmaking journey spanning over three decades. He will speak about his latest film Look Back (2026), presented as a Special Presentation in the Horizon section, alongside his feature film breakthroughs like Maborosi (1995) and After Life (1998); internationally acclaimed works like Nobody Knows (2004), Still Walking (2008) and Shoplifters (2018), and his overseas productions like The Truth (2019) and Broker (2022).


Examining core themes of memory, grief, and unconventional family dynamics on the fringes of society, Koreeda masterfully blends documentary-like realism with gentle human drama that subverts traditional melodrama. Don’t miss this rare opportunity to gain insights from a master filmmaker whose delicate lens continues to inspire generations of cinephiles.


Moderated by: Boo Junfeng, Filmmaker and Chairperson of SGIFF

Conducted in Japanese with English interpretation
events.short_description: Join SGIFF Cinema Honorary Award recipient Hirokazu Koreeda for an intimate journey through over three decades of filmmaking. In this exclusive dialogue, the Japanese master will discuss his deeply humanist approach to storytelling, exploring the nuances of memory, grief, and marginality.

events.name: Artist Spotlight: Ubac Studio
events.description:
Hear from media artist duo Ubac Studio as they walk through how they create XR universes and expand the possibilities of cinematic experiences. Their work, Voooooo---Peeeeee---, a multisensory XR experience, is presented as part of Parallax.


Speaker

Ubac Studio is a Seoul-based media artist duo composed of Hyeunjoo Woo and Jiyun Park. Working primarily with XR-based interactive installations, they explore moments when technology’s construction of the world collides with individual sensory experience. Their works have been presented at Cannes Immersive and Venice Immersive, and received the Festivals Connexion Award at Annecy 2026.

films.name: Amazomania
films.short_description: A 1996 expedition to the Amazon rainforest to make contact with the Korubo people yields huge professional success for journalist Erling Söderström. He meets the tribe again three decades later, only to be confronted by the impact of his ignorance.
films.description:
In 1996, journalist Erling Söderström joins an expedition to the Amazon rainforest to initiate contact with the isolated Korubo tribe, amid rising deadly clashes with settlers. The group leaves after amassing dozens of hours of footage and photographs, which Söderström turns into an award-winning film. Swept up in idyllic memories, he revisits the Korubo three decades later, but is met with demands for reparations and the rights to their images which the tribe never consented for use.


Amazomania interrogates the politics of image-making and the ethics of ethnographic filmmaking, revealing the exploitation that occurs in the name of knowledge. Made with editorial input from the Korubo, it offers a revisionist take on the landmark expedition.

events.name: Beyond the Screen: The Future, Revisited
events.description:
A virtual artist can take the stage. Getting audiences to stay is another production. Spend years putting the future of entertainment on a festival programme and changing jobs comes with an unusual perk—grading your own predictions. Sten Saluveer and Jay Kim revisit the possibilities they championed at Cannes Next and BIFAN XR, now from senior seats at Telia Estonia and Studio Realive, exploring the partnerships, audiences and business decisions that make new entertainment work—and which of their forecasts deserve a second look.


Speaker

Sten Saluveer, Chief Growth & Innovation Officer, Telia Estonia

Sten Saluveer is Chief Growth Officer and Head of Digital Solutions & New Businesses at Telia Estonia, the country's leading ICT and telecommunications company. A futurist, strategist, and educator at the intersection of content, technology, and innovation, Sten's expertise of over two decades spans AI, film & content, and digital sectors across business, governance, and strategy. Sten founded and serves as Head of Studies of the executive-level Mastering AI for European Film Professionals programme at Denmark's National Film School, and is an Advisory Board member of Future Media Hubs, an innovation alliance of 50+ European media companies. He previously served as Head, and now contributes annually to Cannes Next, the innovation track of the Marché du Film — Festival de Cannes, and Director of the Tallinn Digital Summit, hosted by the Prime Minister of Estonia. Sten advises content and technology organisations on AI and digital, and frequently collaborates with governments and the European Commission on innovation, AI, and policy. He has produced half a dozen films and occasionally performs as an electronic musician.


Jay Kim CEO, Studio Realive, SM Entertainment Group

Jay Kim studied literature and film and emerged as a pioneer in immersive media as a founding member of the storytelling studio GiiÖii. He planned and produced global XR projects like Missing Pictures (2022) and expanded the industry's horizons as the curator of the "Beyond Reality" XR section at the Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival. In 2024, Kim joined Studio Realive, a subsidiary of SM Entertainment, as CCO, successfully managing operations across immersive tech, XR, virtual entertainment, and AI technologies. Appointed as the new CEO on March 31, 2026, he is now guiding Studio Realive into its next chapter, driving the company forward at the intersection of technology and art.


Moderator

Wonsun Shin, Curator of Parallax

Wonsun Shin is a freelance consultant with extensive experience in co-production projects, festival strategies, and remake rights acquisitions. She began her career at CJ Entertainment, collaborating with Paramount Pictures and DreamWorks for film marketing. As Director of Film Festival Strategies, she built strong relationships with major festivals, a practice she continues today. Wonsun has been a jury and selection committee member for prestigious project markets and industry programs such as NAFF BIFAN, NFDC Film Bazaar Goa, and Fantastic 7 at Cannes. In 2024, she participated in the Cannes Investors Circle selection committee at Marché du Film and the first round of project selections for the Hubert Bals Fund. Her talent for identifying emerging voices and cultivating global connections has been a defining feature of her professional journey.

films.name: The House on the Moon
films.short_description: In this science-fiction, fantasy, romance and wuxia mashup, the fairy maiden Chang’e embarks on a journey to the moon to find her missing lover and is joined by a bandit from earth.
films.description:
The legendary archer Hou Yi goes missing during a mission to save a dying sun. This prompts his lover, the fairy maiden Chang'e, to embark on a dangerous journey to find him on the dark side of the moon. Along the way, she encounters strange figures, including a bandit from earth who accompanies her on her quest. Their journey leads them to Peng Meng, who has come in search of Chang'e’s last remaining elixir of immortality.


In a genre-defying mix of science-fiction, fantasy, romance and wuxia, The House on the Moon takes on the timeless Chinese legend of Chang'e and Hou Yi and transforms it into a bold, inventive spectacle. Billed as Singapore’s first-ever feature-length wuxia film and the country’s first feature produced using virtual production technology, Nelson Yeo’s highly anticipated sophomore effort challenges expectations of its source material, taking Singaporean cinema to exciting new heights.

events.name: Reading the Room: The Data Behind the Deal
events.description:
Every film is a gamble dressed up as a decision. Largo.ai founder and CEO Sami Arpa explores how script, casting and market data can inform development, financing and distribution—holding forecasts up against real outcomes, including the ones the model got wrong. Discover what audience predictions reveal, where they fall short, and how filmmakers can use them while keeping creative judgement firmly in human hands. Because knowing the odds has never been the same as knowing which film to make.


This programme is supported by the Embassy of Switzerland in Singapore.


Speaker

Sami Arpa, CEO, Largo

Sami Arpa is the CEO and Co-founder of Largo, bridging the gap between artificial intelligence and cinema. A film director and producer with a PhD in Computational Aesthetics from EPFL, Sami is a repeat founder whose previous venture, Sofy.tv, was acquired in 2023.

films.name: Everytime
films.short_description: In this intimate study of grief, a mother, daughter and teenage boy are drawn into the orbit of an absent loved one. They take a trip to a seaside resort, where reality shimmers under the glistening sun and time folds into itself.
films.description:
On the eve of a family holiday, teenager Jessie climbs onto a roof and ventures too close to the edge. A year later, her mother, sister and boyfriend try to live with a semblance of normalcy while still reeling from their devastating loss. Each struggles privately with blame and incomprehension, yet they remain bound together by the gaping hole in their hearts. The unlikely trio embark on the trip that never happened, arriving at a resort where memories of the past collide with the unbearable present.


Featuring adroit cinematography and layered performances, Everytime examines the effects of grief on perception: its strange power to bend time and suspend logic, if only briefly.

films.name: Corporeal Forms: Four Stories
films.short_description: A puppeteer’s hand resurrects the missing and lost bodies of history through four stories in this lecture performance.
films.description:
A puppeteer breaks the joints of a dead sparrow, reanimating it to fly again. From that gesture, Hsu Che-Yu and Chen Wan-Yin move through four stories about what the imagination conjures, told as oblique microhistories: a laboratory rabbit killed for swine fever vaccine; ancestral portraits whose photographed faces sit on reused studio backdrops painted in Eastern gouache; Mongolia’s last wild horses, bred backwards under the Third Reich and today through surrogates; and conjoined twins separated on live television in 1979.


Animated by master puppeteer Kuo Chien-Fu—who works in budaixi (Taiwanese glove puppetry), where the hand inside the puppet revives its soul—the trio invokes the contradictory attachment to restoring the corporeal semblance of lost things. The original performance was commissioned by Theater der Welt and Taipei Performing Arts Center, and premiered at Frankfurt’s Mousonturm.

events.name: Lights, Camera, AI: From Production to Post
events.description:
Filmmaking runs on creative judgment, collaboration and a great many deadlines. Join voices from studio workflows, creative technology and filmmaking to explore where AI earns its keep—from editing to delivery—and what changes on Monday morning, with the people making the films at its centre.


Speakers

Rebeca Cervantes, Sr. Post-production Executive Int. Originals EUX, Amazon MGM Studios

Rebeca Cervantes is a Sr. Post-Production Executive at Amazon MGM Studios, overseeing film and series productions across several territories in Europe including the Nordics. With over 20 years in the industry spanning VFX, production, and gaming, she brings a cross-industry perspective to post-production leveraging emerging technology to streamline creative pipelines at scale.


Chetan Shah, Head – Video Strategic Development, APAC & Japan, Adobe Inc.

Chetan Shah leads Video Strategic Development across APAC and Japan at Adobe, driving growth initiatives with broadcasters, media companies, brands and creative organisations. Chetan helps customers adopt AI-powered workflows through Adobe Firefly, Frame.io and Creative Cloud, leading executive engagements, workshops and innovation programmes that connect emerging technology with real business outcomes.

events.name: From Idea to Production: Inside the Creative Process
events.description:
Every creative project begins with a possibility. Then come the experiments, the revisions and the file optimistically labelled "final." Jessie Hughes and Meg White pair entertainment innovation with hands-on engineering to explore how ideas become working tools and screen experiences. From visual development to prototyping and production, discover how creators test approaches, solve practical problems and hold on to creative intention—because "one more version" is both an opportunity and a scheduling problem.


Speakers

Jessie Hughes, Senior Vice President, Innovation; Endemol Shine Australia

Jessie Hughes is the Senior Vice President, Innovation & Founding Director of the Innovation Lab at Endemol Shine Australia, part of Banijay Entertainment— the world's largest independent content production company with a catalogue exceeding 265,000 hours of programming, including MasterChef, Survivor, Big Brother and Black Mirror. Jessie brings a decade of collaborating with tech giants like Canva, Google, Meta and Leonardo.Ai, designing emergent, imaginative technologies. She’s trained the US Television Academy and Hollywood Professionals Association in AI screen production, and is an awarded new media artist.


Meg White, Chief Technical Officer; Slobberdog

Meg White (PhD) is an engineer, researcher and creative technologist working across intelligent systems and electrical engineering. She is the founder of Slobberdog: a creative and technical R&D Lab bridging hardware, software, and the fuzzy places in between. Exploring how autonomous systems affect human agency, decision-making and the distribution of power, Meg’s research pushes novel workflows and systems that need to be invented before they can be implemented.

films.name: The Compression Zone
films.short_description: A video game descends into a pixel dungeon where demons demand a sacrifice for your data
films.description:
Playing alongside the game’s protagonist, we descend into a techno-pastel dungeon called The Compression Zone, where data demons offer to act as our messengers but demand something in return: a Faustian pact for our times. Homebrewed on the Unity engine and updated at every performance, Shaheer’s video game shifts our focus to the tools of perception in our digitally mediated realities. It unpacks how the algorithmic logics of data infrastructure shape what we see: data is packaged and compiled, deployed across corners of the globe, stretching over land and coursing through undersea fibre-optic lines—leaving imprints on the very environments they render on our screens.


Drawn partly from his move from Lahore to Canada during his growing-up years, the video-game lecture traces the expansion of cartographic imagination precipitated by the early internet. At the same time, it explores how the convenience of instant knowledge rests on compression algorithms that make a value judgement about what counts as ‘loss’ in the process.

films.name: Look Back
films.short_description: Fujino draws to be seen, while Kyomoto draws to hide. Together they make manga, and discover what art can and cannot hold.
films.description:
Outgoing and sure of her gift, Fujino is the star of her elementary school paper—her four-panel comics bring great delight to her classmates. One day Kyomoto, a shut-in, gets a comic slot as well, and Fujino realises that Kyomoto’s drawings are far beyond anything she can achieve. Envy hardens into obsession; though no matter how hard Fujino tries, she is unable to reach Kyomoto’s level.


When the two girls finally meet, their rivalry turns into something rarer: a friendship that blossoms as their manga journeys take flight. Yet when the chance to create a serial arrives, it pulls them in different directions. What becomes of a friendship built on the page?


Adapted from Tatsuki Fujimoto’s acclaimed one-shot manga, Look Back returns Hirokazu Kore-eda to the register he knows best: children observed at close range, over time, with patience rather than sentiment. Trading animation’s stylisation for his signature naturalism, he lets the two protagonists simply grow up on camera, in the intimacy of 35mm film.

films.name: Imagination + The Rest Is My Ghost
films.short_description: Film grain, spectral beams and low-frequency murmurs: two artists converse in light and sound, channelling the sublime.
films.description:
Imagination opens this double bill of light and sound. Among the ruins of Japan’s oldest film laboratory were voluminous century-old 35mm and 16mm reels that had been developed but never exposed. Takashi Makino scanned them at 8K for their materiality alone, which gave him nothing but grain in constant motion. Turning from these decayed reels towards a vaster emptiness, he layered the grainy remains of images with over 30,000 photographs of a cloudless sky shot from the roof of the ruins. Lawrence English accompanies Makino’s visuals with a virtuosic performance, expanding the physical experience of emptiness with the sonic sublime.


The second billing, The Rest Is My Ghost, is the final instalment of a trilogy by English, after Cruel Optimism and Wilderness of Mirrors. He uses processed field recordings, synthesis and amplified low-frequency noise as his response to what he calls ‘acid nostalgia’: the past’s hauntings flattened and weaponised in the current political mood. Makino responds intuitively with spectral beams of light penetrating the haze, dancing with the prophetic sounds of a ruinous world. Acting as each other’s muse, they craft a luminous performance that invites us to experience the weight of nothingness and the fullness of being.

films.name: Paper Tiger
films.short_description: A modest father in 1980s New York and his unremarkable family find their lives upturned by a get-rich scheme gone wrong. This textured crime thriller is anchored in performances that underscore the grandness, despair and humanity of wanting more.
films.description:
The Pearls, an unremarkable family in a 1980s New York suburb, live cordially, though sometimes anxious about money. Unlike his headstrong wife, Irwin is lamblike and easily swayed—especially when his flashy brother Gary comes knocking with a lucrative business idea. When the brothers’ eagerness to make bank ensnares all of them in a murky Russian group, the true price of their aspirations becomes clear.


James Gray, a longtime chronicler of retro America, serves up a crime thriller but tempers the genre’s excesses for an elegant human scale. With its celluloid textures and heavyweight performances, where strains in a voice feel like a cocked gun, Paper Tiger is a tactile exploration of the American Dream in its brilliant, brutal twilight.

films.name: Nowhere to Lay My Eyes
films.short_description: An experimental filmmaker’s reunion with her mother after a decade’s absence hides a quietly transformative quality in this ruminative work in Hong’s prolific oeuvre.
films.description:
Experimental filmmaker Sang-hee, accompanied by her brother, visits her mother on Jeju Island after a decade’s absence. She meets her documentarian stepfather and her younger, aspiring artist stepsister for the first time. Marked by awkward niceties and blink-and-you’ll-miss microexpressions, the tension in the mother–daughter reunion remains oblique. Family conversations flit naturally between artmaking, beauty, and even the notion of eternity.


Slim yet profound, this is a particularly ruminative work in Hong’s prolific oeuvre. While it glides across surfaces and impressions to reveal hidden interiorities as his films tend to do, the revelation here seems to hit harder: eternities lasting mere moments, waiting quietly to be laid eyes on, and felt.

films.name: La Bola Negra
films.short_description: Across epochs—Republican Spain in 1932, the Civil War in 1937 and contemporary Madrid in 2017—three men navigate historical turmoil and repression, connected by love, loss and literature, in this sweeping work of queer cinema.
films.description:
In Republican Spain in 1932, a young man applies for membership at a local casino and is rejected. During the Civil War in 1937, a conscripted musician looks after a wounded prisoner and builds a friendship with him. In modern-day Spain in 2017, a historian learns of his grandfather’s death and receives an unexpected inheritance. 


In La Bola Negra, nearly a century of Spanish political history enfolds the lives of these young men whose desires to be seen and accepted are thwarted by society’s conservatism. Directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi take inspiration from Federico García Lorca’s unfinished text La bola negra and Alberto Conejero’s play La piedra oscura, mixing real-life and fictional characters in this sweeping work of queer cinema.

films.name: Brave Cat
films.short_description: A young forest cat embarks on a courageous journey to find her mother, joined by new friends also searching for lost family.
films.description:
Animals have been disappearing from the forest, kidnapped by the human—a giant monster who forces them to join his circus. Years after witnessing her mother’s abduction by the human’s guard dogs, Kona, a young cat, gathers the courage to search for her.


Traversing woodland and glaciers, venturing all the way out to sea, Kona embarks on a transformative journey accompanied by Colin, a puppy abandoned by the guard dogs due to his disability, and Bernard, a plucky big bear who repeatedly escapes from the circus. Chased by the guard dogs and faced with the challenge of navigating unfamiliar environments, they bond over their shared hope of reuniting with lost family.


In this uplifting adventure, friendship fosters the strength to stand together and put an end to terror. Filled with wonder and heart, Brave Cat is a richly textured work of animation that tells an empathetic story about loss and forgiveness, reflecting imaginatively upon the universal theme of human rights.

events.name: In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones

films.name: In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones
films.short_description: In this campus satire set in 1970s Delhi, a ragtag group of architecture students express their restless idealism against a system that rewards conformity and punishes dissent.
films.description:
In an architecture institute in Delhi, a ragtag group of students bungle their way as they submit their thesis before graduation. Among them is Anand ‘Annie’ Grover, who is repeating his fifth year for the fourth time and dreams of designing an architecture project that would bring about social change.


In her first screenplay credit, Booker Prize-winning novelist Arundhati Roy took inspiration from her time as an architecture student, depicting college life in the 1970s with sharp satirical wit. Pradip Krishen lovingly captures the countercultural atmosphere of the zeitgeist: the anarchic, restless energy of youthful idealism clashing with hegemonic systems that seek to protect the status quo—all while Beatles tunes play on.

films.description: A Grindr match sends two men from Singapore across the border for a night away from prying eyes—but something shifts as their gaze turns inwards onto themselves.

films.name: Her Silence
films.description: When the parents of an international student visit her in Sydney, she contends with her mother’s quiet disapproval of her life there. Familial tensions are wrapped in reticence and slight gestures in this family drama.

films.name: Son Of A
films.description: When a Vietnamese child mysteriously shows up at James and his father’s hawker stall, the two men handle the situation differently, with the child’s fate hanging in the balance.

films.name: What Remains at Dawn
films.description: In Singapore, executions happen at dawn. Across a decade of border crossings, appeals and silence, two sisters fight to save their brother as he writes poetry from death row.

films.name: Fujiko
films.short_description: 1970s, Japan. Former disco dancer Fujiko finds her groove as a single mother after reclaiming her baby from her in-laws. Fusing an irreverent rock ’n’ roll spirit with comedy, the drama celebrates independence in a patriarchal society.
films.description:
In 1970s Japan, Fujiko takes the unconventional route of becoming a single mother after reclaiming her infant who was forcibly taken away by her in-laws. Her decision is met with derision by unsympathetic family members, while the lack of childcare facilities leaves her with less time to work, thrusting her into dire situations. Yet Fujiko remains determined; she encounters warmth and support when she least expects, allowing her to create the life she envisions for her family.


Set against the backdrop of the women’s movement resurgence in Japan, Fujiko fuses an irreverent rock ’n’ roll spirit with comedy as it charts the path of a woman finding her groove as an independent woman in a patriarchal society.

events.name: Baby Jackfruit Baby Guava
events.description: This screening includes a Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: Baby Jackfruit Baby Guava
films.short_description: With humour and heart, a queer filmmaker turns the camera on his family, revealing how love, identity and belonging are reshaped in contemporary Vietnam.
films.description:
Long-buried tensions, unspoken identities and unresolved love have shaped filmmaker Nông Nhật Quang’s family for years. When a new chapter in his older sister Mai's life begins, the fragile balance that has held the family together starts to shift, prompting Quang to turn the camera towards his kin.


Believing that filmmaking can open conversations where words have failed, Quang retraces his changing bond with Mai, reflects on his own journey as a gay son, and gently navigates the fraught relationship between his mother and sister. Intimate and deeply compassionate, Baby Jackfruit Baby Guava invites audiences into a Vietnamese family who are learning to give voice to years of silence.


The film assembles family photographs, diaries, phone recordings and home videos into a vibrant first-person documentary where memories collide with the present. With candid observation, sharp humour and queer exuberance, Nông embraces the camera not as a tool of objectivity but as a way of speaking to his loved ones. An emerging voice in Vietnamese queer cinema, he captures a generation negotiating greater LGBTQ+ visibility in a society where the hardest conversations still begin at home.
