films.name: Julián
films.short_description: New kid on the block Julián spends the summer with his grandmother and discovers the magic of the ocean when he decides to dress up for the Coney Island Mermaid Parade.
films.description:
Seven-year-old Julián spends the summer with his no-nonsense Dominican American grandmother Carmela in New York City, where he is introduced to his Caribbean heritage and the bustling Brooklyn community. When his new friends invite him to join them at the Coney Island Mermaid Parade, Julián recruits Carmela to make him a mermaid costume. Though he eventually finds that not everyone believes in his dream to become a mermaid, Julián is determined to make waves with the help of a magical ocean spirit.


An adaptation of the award-winning picture book, Julián Is a Mermaid, the film is rendered in 2D-animation in marker and coloured pencil style with a zesty palette. With Julián, animation studio Cartoon Saloon adds yet another lovingly crafted animation to their acclaimed filmography of whimsical and meaningful stories.

films.name: Corporeal Forms: Four Stories
films.short_description: A puppeteer’s hand resurrects the missing and lost bodies of history through four stories in this lecture performance.
films.description:
A puppeteer breaks the joints of a dead sparrow, reanimating it to fly again. From that gesture, Hsu Che-Yu and Chen Wan-Yin move through four stories about what the imagination conjures, told as oblique microhistories: a laboratory rabbit killed for swine fever vaccine; ancestral portraits whose photographed faces sit on reused studio backdrops painted in Eastern gouache; Mongolia’s last wild horses, bred backwards under the Third Reich and today through surrogates; and conjoined twins separated on live television in 1979.


Animated by master puppeteer Kuo Chien-Fu—who works in budaixi (Taiwanese glove puppetry), where the hand inside the puppet revives its soul—the trio invokes the contradictory attachment to restoring the corporeal semblance of lost things. The original performance was commissioned by Theater der Welt and Taipei Performing Arts Center, and premiered at Frankfurt’s Mousonturm.

events.name: Mariinka
events.description: This screening includes a Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: Mariinka
films.short_description: The lives of childhood neighbours—a promising boxer, a young orphan and four brothers—intersect, implode and diverge across a decade of war in this stirring documentary of the battle in Mariinka, a destroyed city in eastern Ukraine.
films.description:
The Ukrainian city of Mariinka in Donetsk has been under siege by Russian forces since 2014. Natasha, a promising young boxer, suspends her dreams to become a paramedic. Angela, orphaned and separated from her sisters, survives by couriering items to both fronts under fire. While Mark and Ruslan fight for opposing sides in the city they grew up in, their youngest brother Daniil follows the conflict from the US and dreams of following in their footsteps.


The documentary scales the personal cost of war with the destruction of an entire city, capturing the lost dreams and potential of Mariinka’s inhabitants. Shot on 16mm film for over a decade, this immersive portrait of Mariinka is at once a commemoration and lament for a city that once was.

events.name: Imagination + The Rest Is My Ghost
events.description: This event includes a Q&A session with the performers.

films.name: Imagination + The Rest Is My Ghost
films.short_description: Film grain, spectral beams and low-frequency murmurs: two artists converse in light and sound, channelling the sublime.
films.description:
Imagination opens this double bill of light and sound. Among the ruins of Japan’s oldest film laboratory were voluminous century-old 35mm and 16mm reels that had been developed but never exposed. Takashi Makino scanned them at 8K for their materiality alone, which gave him nothing but grain in constant motion. Turning from these decayed reels towards a vaster emptiness, he layered the grainy remains of images with over 30,000 photographs of a cloudless sky shot from the roof of the ruins. Lawrence English accompanies Makino’s visuals with a virtuosic performance, expanding the physical experience of emptiness with the sonic sublime.


The second billing, The Rest Is My Ghost, is the final instalment of a trilogy by English, after Cruel Optimism and Wilderness of Mirrors. He uses processed field recordings, synthesis and amplified low-frequency noise as his response to what he calls ‘acid nostalgia’: the past’s hauntings flattened and weaponised in the current political mood. Makino responds intuitively with spectral beams of light penetrating the haze, dancing with the prophetic sounds of a ruinous world. Acting as each other’s muse, they craft a luminous performance that invites us to experience the weight of nothingness and the fullness of being.

films.name: All of a Sudden
films.short_description: Enveloped in care and tenderness, the conversations between a Paris nursing home director and a dying Japanese playwright become a space for gradual transformation.
films.description:
Marie-Lou runs a nursing home outside Paris, struggling against a system that treats care as a cost to be minimised. When she encounters Mari, a Japanese playwright who is terminally ill, the two begin a series of conversations that bridge the cultural, personal and emotional distances between them. Each exchange, marked by shared curiosity and admiration, expands to hold these differences.


All of a Sudden is built around long, unhurried dialogue, where conversations become a transformative space. As it moves between art, performance and companionship, the film explores a radical idea of care: attention, listening and presence as acts of resistance in systems that prize efficiency over genuine connection.

films.name: Possible Love
films.short_description: A working-class family and a wealthy couple become entangled as they make a documentary together. Tensions simmer and loyalties shift in Lee Chang-dong’s exquisite, slow-burn drama, which asks if the distance between people can ever be closed.
films.description:
Blue-collar worker Ho-seok is left broken by a wave of layoffs and a violently repressed strike. He refuses therapy, while his wife Mi-ok holds down a factory job and keeps their family together. They become subjects of a documentary when Mi-ok befriends filmmaker Ye-ji, who senses dramatic potential in their pain. Backed by her rich husband, Ye-ji insinuates herself and her camera into their lives.


As the working class and the wealthy cross paths, desire and envy, fascination and appropriation shade into one another. Anchored by a stellar cast, this finely observed drama examines the fragile ideal of solidarity and the fraught quest for intimacy, asking if the distance between any two individuals can ever be closed.

films.name: Rose
films.short_description: A battle-scarred soldier arrives at a village, with an inheritance and a deep secret about their identity. Sandra Hüller spellbindingly leads this compact period saga about the violence of gender norms as well as the utopias of desire that cannot be contained.
films.description:
In seventeenth-century Germany, returning soldier Rose arrives at a tiny Protestant village, with a battle-scarred smile and a deed to farmland. Though Rose’s enigmatic identity raises eyebrows, the village folk come to respect Rose as a God-fearing, noble gentleman. But when betrothed to another landowner’s daughter, a secret beneath Rose’s persona comes under devastating scrutiny.


Anchored by Sandra Hüller’s spellbinding, shapeshifting performance, this period saga is told with impeccable balance. The pared-down but precise screenplay lays bare the violence of a society ruled by gender norms. Yet at the same time, the protagonists’ indomitable desires conjure a quiet, queer dignity that commands its own authority.

films.name: Rehearsals for a Revolution
films.short_description: Through five generations of personal stories, this documentary reveals how memories of resistance survive beyond political upheavals. A poetic portrait of Iran’s ongoing struggle, it explores storytelling and everyday acts of defiance as quiet forms of revolution.
films.description:
Through five intimate portraits, Pegah Ahangarani revisits 50 years of Iran’s history, revealing how political upheavals reverberate across generations. Beginning with her father’s journey from revolutionary idealism to disillusionment, the film follows her uncle’s hopes for reform, her teacher’s encounter with repression, Ahangarani’s political awakening during the 2009 Green Movement, and the new possibilities embodied by her young daughter.


The film blends family archives, photographs, recordings and historical footage into a poetic documentary essay. Through recollection and reassembling fragments of the past, Ahangarani explores storytelling, remembrance and artistic expression as quieter forms of revolution.

events.name: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma

films.name: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
films.short_description: The road to a queer woman’s sexual awakening is paved with geysers of blood and radical vulnerability, powered by fantasy and imagination. Guilty pleasures have never felt more seen in this healing, tonally surprising take on the slasher genre.
films.description:
Geeky queer filmmaker Kris is tasked with reviving the Camp Miasma slasher franchise, with the goal of rehabilitating its transphobic reputation. She ventures into a remote campground to meet with the reclusive and enchanting Billy, who played the ‘final girl’ in the original film, hoping to persuade her to take on a cameo. Over spliffs, fried chicken and supermarket snacks, the two women bond, culminating in an ecstatic sexual awakening.


With copious stylistic throwbacks to definitive ’80s and ’90s horror, Jane Schoenberg’s third feature is packed with flesh and fluids while remaining tonally surprising. It resolutely celebrates libidinal liberation by giving space to raucous fantasies and freeing pleasures from guilty prison.

films.name: Nowhere to Lay My Eyes
films.short_description: An experimental filmmaker’s reunion with her mother after a decade’s absence hides a quietly transformative quality in this ruminative work in Hong’s prolific oeuvre.
films.description:
Experimental filmmaker Sang-hee, accompanied by her brother, visits her mother on Jeju Island after a decade’s absence. She meets her documentarian stepfather and her younger, aspiring artist stepsister for the first time. Marked by awkward niceties and blink-and-you’ll-miss microexpressions, the tension in the mother–daughter reunion remains oblique. Family conversations flit naturally between artmaking, beauty, and even the notion of eternity.


Slim yet profound, this is a particularly ruminative work in Hong’s prolific oeuvre. While it glides across surfaces and impressions to reveal hidden interiorities as his films tend to do, the revelation here seems to hit harder: eternities lasting mere moments, waiting quietly to be laid eyes on, and felt.

events.name: On Memories of Countless Days Away
events.description: This screening includes a Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: On Memories of Countless Days Away
films.short_description: Two friends recall their childhoods in Singapore, revisit their earlier films and perform a dance for which no recording remains. Their musings and archives are woven together in a meditation on how memories are not recovered, but composed anew.
films.description:
Two longtime friends revisit their formative years as artists and their coming of age in Singapore. Piecing together footage accumulated over the years and reconstructing a dance for which no archive remains, they sit with failure, doubt and the creative possibilities that persist. Their thoughts turn towards the fraught question of where they belong: one traces a journey to his ancestral grave, the other reckons with the quiet erasure of her father’s citizenship.


Unfolding with the logic of a dance, the film shifts fluidly between past and present, Singapore and Japan. What emerges is a graceful, vulnerable meditation on memory as an act of composition.

events.name: Four Seasons in Java
events.description: This screening includes a Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: Four Seasons in Java
films.short_description: In this atmospheric magical realist drama, a Javanese woman is released after 20 years in prison and returns to her hometown. Her unwanted presence forces her to face the four seasons of her past and confront the village’s covert powers and injustice.
films.description:
After serving 20 years in prison for murdering an accomplice to her rape as a 16-year-old, Pertiwi returns home to an uneasy reunion with her parents and hostility from chauvinistic male authority figures. Even as she copes with the lingering effects of trauma, the resolute Pertiwi forms solidarity with fellow outcasts, offering them shelter and community. A deaf-mute teenager whose experiences uncannily mirror her own pushes Pertiwi to seek justice.


Like her past features, Andini centres stoic female characters and continues to confront deep-rooted misogyny, violence and abuse of power. However, she now veers into fantastical elements that represent truth and power in this unflinching magical realist drama that lays bare societal ills.

films.name: Shame and Money
films.short_description: A family in rural Kosovo leave their farm to find work in the capital. Mired in familial obligation, caregiving and financial precarity, their survival becomes dependent on the whims of strangers.
films.description:
Shaban is an honest dairy farmer and the head of his family. When a family dispute forces the family to seek work in the city, they are aided by wealthy relatives who promise them a secure future. But as Shaban faces prolonged job insecurity and humiliating incidents, he becomes increasingly dissociated and begins to lose control of his impulses.


Recalling the brutal social realities of Italian neorealism and Indian Parallel Cinema, the film follows a man’s desperation to support his family and maintain his dignity. Shame and Money shows the debilitating erasure of self-worth in a hypercapitalist era, where money determines one’s place in society and only the rich find meagre work shameful.

events.name: Gaza’s Twins, Come Back to Me
events.description: This screening includes an online Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: Gaza’s Twins, Come Back to Me
films.short_description: Forcibly separated from her premature twins in a hospital at the start of the Gaza war, a mother juggles between raising four small children, attempting to reunite with her babies, and survival in the midst of a brutal siege.
films.description:
After one of her triplets dies at birth, Rania loses contact with her surviving infants Jowan and Hamoud when they are evacuated to the south of Gaza. Stuck in the north, Rania enlists her family to take the twins in after identifying them on social media. As the cost of essential goods skyrockets and medical supplies are withheld, Hamoud begins to show signs of long-term illness while his mother seeks opportunities to bring them home.


Unfolding over 16 months, this documentary portrays a mother’s longing for her children, against the devastation wreaked upon a city. In the unrelenting genocide of Palestinians, Gaza’s Twins shows that even survival may be little comfort as civilians contend with the crippling effects of trauma and untreated medical conditions.

films.name: Vertiginous
films.short_description: Jacques wakes Bruno up at daybreak to deliver a life-changing revelation: nothing is real—they are living in a simulation and he has the evidence to prove it. Struck by existential vertigo, Bruno soon reaps the benefits of this discovery.
films.description:
Jacques arrives at his friend Bruno’s house with the steadfast conviction that the world is a simulation. He has collected 264 observations of glitches in reality and finds his 265th when Bruno’s wife goes into labour and their daughter slips out without an umbilical cord. By the end of the strange day, an initially sceptical Bruno is fully convinced and soon finds a way to hack this new understanding of reality.


Rendered in low-poly 3D animation typically seen in old video games, the film’s aesthetic adds another layer of antirealism. In typical Dupieux fashion, Vertiginous pokes fun at existential philosophising and explores gags that live in the cracks of artifice, troubling the boundaries between physical and digital reality.

events.name: [Visionary Encounters] Yim Soon-Rye — Craft, Curiousity, Care.
events.description:
In-depth discussion with Yim Soon-rye, the leading Korean woman film director who this year also heads the SGIFF main competition jury. With a directing career that stretches more than 25 years, Yim has become known for social issues-driven films, an unhurried and unflustered style and a gentle, personal approach. Operating on the indie wing of Korean cinema, Yim has often told female-driven stories and become a pioneer woman filmmaker in a male-dominated and hierarchical Korean industry. The discussion will also illuminate the overseas influences, such as her European education and admiration of Japan’s Mizoguchi Kenzo, that shaped her work.


Speaker

Yim Soon-Rye, Director & Screenwriter, South Korea


Modetator

Thong Kay Wee, SGIFF Programme Director
events.short_description: A respected Korean indie filmmaker sheds light on the highs and lows of a directing career outside the commercial mainstream. A must for young and aspiring filmmakers (and anyone trying to second guess the competition prizes).

events.name: [Roundtables] Screenwriters Roundtable
events.description:
Three writer-directors, whose latest features have enjoyed wide international impact this year, discuss their different journeys and varying levels of experience. They include first timer Ang with Ah Girl, through self-taught Juyal, who made shorts and documentaries before this year delivering his debut feature The Ink Stained Hand and the Missing Thumb, through to the more established Andini with her Four Seasons in Java. Andini’s work straddles social issues and accessible genres and in 2023 included the Netflix series Cigarette Girl.


The discussion will examine the screenwriting and development processes in Asia, how to give and take notes, and the various requirements that come with trying to make a co-produceable script. It will also look at making the leap from short films and documentaries to fiction features (and narrative series). And tackle the value of participating in labs and workshops and how to get the best out of mentorship.


Panelists

Ang Geck Geck (Priscilla), Director & Screenwriter, Singapore

Kamila Andinii, Director, Screenwriter, Producer, Indonesia

Yashasvi Juyal, Director and cinematographer, India


Moderator

Kris Ong, Screenwriter & Secretary of Screenwriters Association (Singapore)
events.short_description: Dive into the process of screenwriting and doing what it takes to make an award-winning first feature.

events.name: 9 Temples To Heaven
events.description: This screening includes a Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: 9 Temples to Heaven
films.short_description: Faced with the imminent death of his mother, a man leads three generations of his family on a single-day temple pilgrimage—where prayer meets doubt, and reason wrestles with superstition.
films.description:
When a middle-aged businessman learns that his mother’s death is imminent, he packs the entire family of nine into a van for a single-day pilgrimage to nine temples, hoping to gain enough merit to alter her fate. But the road trip soon becomes fraught: old wounds resurface, alongside generational tension, marital strife, and clashing views on faith and modernity. As the matriarch begins to tire, the family reckon with their fractures and the reality of aging.


Drifting effortlessly between scientific rationality, spiritual recourse and the inevitability of mortality, the camera moves like a floating consciousness through architecture and landscapes. What emerges is a restrained commentary on Buddhist culture while the search for rationality crumbles.

events.name: [Roundtables] The Architecture of Opportunity: Grants, Coproduction, and the Making of a Global Cinema
events.description:
National film funds built for a twentieth century industry now operate inside a production and distribution environment reshaped by platforms and emerging technologies. Careers across Asia and Europe are increasingly transnational by design. This roundtable discusses how grants (including those for project or talent development) are infrastructure for coproduction, shaping who travels, who collaborates, and whose work circulates internationally. Commissioners from across Asia and Europe discuss how their funds are built to construct sustainable, global careers rather than isolated opportunities, and how coproduction functions as a form of industry capability building. They will address the risks they anticipate for their industries, how their criteria protect diversity and innovation, and how they are responding to new production technologies while keeping human creativity at the center.


Panelists

Manajemen Talenta Nasional (MTN), Indonesia

Centre National de la Cinematographie, France

Cinecittà, Italy

Film Development Council of the Philippines

IMDA, Singapore


Moderator

Jeremy Chua, SGIFF Executive Director

events.name: The Ink-Stained Hand and the Missing Thumb
events.description: This screening includes a Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: The Ink-Stained Hand and the Missing Thumb
films.short_description: Toll operators and lovers Santosh and Rajji spend their days waiting and working in decrepit booths. A tragic accident upturns their quiet lives in this magical realist love story of grief and acceptance.
films.description:
Rajji and Santosh are toll booth operators in the North Indian town of Nagina. The lovers spend slow days in decrepit booths accompanied by a science TV channel while dreaming of a better future. Just as their job demands them to be on the move often, the infrastructure around them sees continual transformation. When a sudden tragedy spawns a beguiling resurrection, the lives of Rajji and Santosh are also irreversibly changed.


Drawing from his experiences growing up in the upper Himalayas where the supernatural exists comfortably within the realm of reality, Yashasvi Juyal presents a magical realist love story that gently unfolds in layers of time and space, anchored by profound feelings of grief.

events.name: Acting in Singapore, Acting from Singapore
events.description:
We see them on our screens, but do we know what they really feel? Join some of our most beloved local film actors as they go off-script and spill the tea on what it truly takes to build an acting career in Singapore.


In this candid roundtable moderated by veteran actress Janice Koh, performers behind iconic Singaporean films share what they look for in directorial collaborations, the dream roles they are still waiting to play, and the conscious choices they make as a Singaporean actor performing for local and international audiences.


If the film industry has ever felt like a mysterious black box, this session offers an intimate, honest look behind the curtain at what it means to act—and belong—here today.


—


Moderated by: Janice Koh, Actor and Vocal Coach

Janice Koh is a celebrated Singaporean actress with over 30 years of stage and screen acting experience. She has participated in international co-productions that have toured to festivals and performing venues worldwide, including Paris, Tokyo, Berlin, and Edinburgh.


A former Nominated Member of Parliament, Janice currently co-chairs theatre company, Wild Rice, and is a co-founder of social enterprise, Pasar Glamour. Janice is a certified Fitzmaurice Voicework teacher, and coaches voice and communications in the corporate sector. In 2022, the French government honoured her with the title of Chevalier des Arts et des Lettres (Knight of the Arts and Letters) for her contributions to the arts.
events.short_description: Step behind the curtain with Singapore’s film actors in a candid roundtable hosted by Janice Koh. Uncover the realities of building a screen career, performing for global audiences and what it means to belong in local cinema today.

events.name: My Name Ain't Suzie
events.description: This screening includes a Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: My Name Ain't Suzie
films.short_description: Shui Mei leaves her fishing village for the city, attracted by the seemingly glamorous life of a prostitute. Across three decades, from the raucous heyday of bars serving foreign soldiers to their quiet wane, she defiantly forges her own path.
films.description:
In the late 1950s, bars and brothels flourish in the Wan Chai district of Hong Kong, catering to American and British soldiers on leave. When the madame of Lucky Bar arrives to scout for new girls from her fishing village, Shui Mei jumps at this coveted opportunity. Through the decades of a changing Hong Kong, Shui Mei’s vivacious spirit and entrepreneurial mindset tide her through the physical hardship and loneliness of her occupation.


Emphasising a female-centred perspective on sex work, My Name Ain’t Suzie is Angie Chen’s response to the sexist and orientalist The World of Suzie Wong (1960). Gritty realities emerge from under neon-lit splendour and practised charm, telling a story of resilience and mutual care.

events.name: Sleep No More
events.description: This screening includes a Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: Sleep No More
films.short_description: Two sisters attempt to uncover the truth of their mother’s death amid possessions and hauntings in a wig factory. Indonesian director Edwin’s foray into horror highlights the systematic exploitation of workers through grotesque means.
films.description:
After Putri and Ida’s mother dies mysteriously at her workplace, the sisters replace her at the wig factory to pay off debts. As exhausted workers pull endless shifts under the watchful eyes of their boss, a slew of hair-raising supernatural encounters unfold. While deaths and possessions mount, their brother Bona, who has a special ability to regenerate body parts, becomes embroiled in the factory happenings.


Sleep No More draws strongly from ’80s Indonesian horror with its analogue visual effects and comical absurdity, and uses an oppressive spatial design to channel a deep sense of unease. The director’s first foray into horror presents an entertaining yet searing social commentary on the true demon of our times—capitalism.

events.name: The Burning Giants
events.description: This screening includes a Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: The Burning Giants
films.short_description: Along the Thai-Myanmar border, a mysterious illness marks Karen bodies with burns and an activist is killed for defending his village’s land, all while a toxic haze spreads across Western Thailand.
films.description:
A Karen man is picked up by forestry officers, his body marked by strange burns no doctor can explain, and taken to a quarantine facility. Elsewhere, drawing on a real-life killing, an Indigenous rights activist is chased from his village and dies for opposing its forced eviction. As a toxic haze creeps towards Thailand’s migrant workers, these separate lives are gradually revealed to be intertwined.


The Burning Giants unfolds without a single protagonist to anchor our gaze. Through measured cinematography, the film builds an immersive and atmospheric world with a magical realist register. The haunting sound design evokes the dread and grief that the images leave unsaid, allowing maladies, otherness and displacement to emerge from the smog with pointed social urgency.

events.name: [Visionary Encounters] Koji Fukada: Japan’s Master of Understated Chaos
events.description:
Still considered as a rising star in his native Japan, director Koji Fukada has achieved plenty already. He made a splash with his first films Human Comedy in Tokyo and Hospitalite, in 2008 and 2010, and won the jury prize in Cannes with his 2016 title Harmonium. Just 42 at the time, in 2022, he was awarded the Tokyo IFF’s Akira Kurosawa award, having hailed him as a meticulous and realistic reflector of modern society. Nagi Notes, his latest effort, which was his first in main competition at Cannes and plays in the SGIFF’s Horizon strand, continues that approach and depicts a consequential week in the life of two women and two children as they figure out what they need to be happy. Expect the conversation to dive into Fukada’s self-described obsession with the French New Wave films of Eric Rohmer, to probe other early career influences, including the director’s time working in animation and live theatre, and to ask how festivals affect the filmmakers they showcase.


Speaker

Koji Fukada, Film director, Japan


Moderator

TBC
events.short_description: Get close to one of Japan’s most thoughtful major auteurs.

events.name: [Visionary Encounters] Capsicums, Colour and Craft: Understanding Cinematography With Akiko Ashizawa
events.description:
Akiko Ashizawa originally wanted to be a director, but for a woman breaking into the sector was no easy task. And, working on commercials as a cinematographer, she soon found that she was able to use light and lenses to tell stories. The prestigious Pierre Angenieux organisation that this year made Ashizawa only its second ever female prize-winner hailed her “mastery of natural light and atmosphere, [and excellence] at capturing complex emotional tones on screen.” Her breakthrough into the movie mainstream and to international acclaim came in 2005 with the beginning of an eight-film partnership with director Kurosawa Kiyoshi. That has made her especially known for shooting atmospheric genre films, but the reality is that she has worked across just about every genre. She also mastered the film-to-digital transition by coming up with many of her own technology solutions. Make sure to also catch the SGIFF screening of Sleep No More, which she shot for Indonesia’s Edwin.


Speaker

Akiko Ashizawa, Cinematographer, Japan


Moderator

films.name: Rose
films.short_description: A battle-scarred soldier arrives at a village, with an inheritance and a deep secret about their identity. Sandra Hüller spellbindingly leads this compact period saga about the violence of gender norms as well as the utopias of desire that cannot be contained.
films.description:
In seventeenth-century Germany, returning soldier Rose arrives at a tiny Protestant village, with a battle-scarred smile and a deed to farmland. Though Rose’s enigmatic identity raises eyebrows, the village folk come to respect Rose as a God-fearing, noble gentleman. But when betrothed to another landowner’s daughter, a secret beneath Rose’s persona comes under devastating scrutiny.


Anchored by Sandra Hüller’s spellbinding, shapeshifting performance, this period saga is told with impeccable balance. The pared-down but precise screenplay lays bare the violence of a society ruled by gender norms. Yet at the same time, the protagonists’ indomitable desires conjure a quiet, queer dignity that commands its own authority.

events.name: [Visionary Encounters] Getting Real About Virtual Reality
events.description:
Sunny Sarnkingthong, producer, director of photography and co-founder of Final Pixel, was part of the recent mega-production Alien: Earth, which was shot in Thailand. Drawing on case studies from his recent projects, he will explore the applications, possibilities, and future potential of virtual production, including insights from his experience working with Sony's OCELLUS camera tracking system. He will explain how the technology is evolving; where it intersects with AI; how VP changes the dynamics and crewing of a film shoot; and how it can be budget-friendly in an Asian context.


Speaker

Sunny Sarnkingthong, Co-founder of Final Pixel Virtual Production studio.

Patrick Frater

films.name: Zoom In, Zoom Out
films.short_description: A game designer searches for his missing roommate through chat logs, avatars and secondhand memory, only to discover that digital remains reveal little of another person.
films.description:
Shi, a video game designer, searches for his missing roommate Gao, and his only clues lie inside a game Gao used to play. The trail leads Shi to YY, Gao’s former love interest, and the two sort through his digital remains: saved conversations, a character still active somewhere, and scattered memories.


Zoom In, Zoom Out is a formal exercise in the possibilities that emerge when film and game languages bleed into each other. It asks how we can hold onto a loved one when they exist mostly as digital fragments, chat logs, avatars, and whether reassembling them counts as memory or something closer to invention. Zooming in and out, as a way of looking in the film, reveals each time the limitations of seeing others and ourselves.

events.name: [Visionary Encounters] Scenes from a Menage: Tom Harari on Making Genre Films With His Brother
events.description:

In Singapore with Cannes competition title L’Inconnue (The Unknown), directed by his younger brother Arthur, Tom Harari will analyse how he transposed a scene from a graphic novel into a live-action film. He will also give a technical breakdown of the pair’s work on the Philippines-set, Japanese-themed WWII film Onoda, 10,000 Nights in the Jungle, in which a solo Japanese soldier refuses to end his own WWII battles.

Tom Harari, Cinematographer, Composer & Screenwriter, France

films.short_description: Taken in by a tribe of lost adolescents, a runaway girl finds a new existence amid freedom and despair. This explosive feature pulls no aesthetic punches, serving up the smouldering, sparkling ruins of youthful abandon in a mixed-media feast.
films.description:
Fleeing a family of religious zealots, Jurie is taken in by a gang of lost adolescents in a Tokyo entertainment quarter. Open to anyone “with emptiness”, they prowl and hustle in streets that thrive on anonymity and addiction. Jurie quickly finds her place in the tribe, but her new life of sheer, unruly freedom soon admits desperation and darkness in equal measure.

films.description:
In a remote Nepalese village nestled deep in the forest, Pirati leads a house of Kinnar women, an ancient third-gender community. The Kinnar are both revered and feared for they are believed to have the power to bless or curse. events.name: Transforming the Local
events.description:
What makes a Singaporean film feel culturally authentic when it's made with international money and stars?


Singapore has always been a crossroads of cultures and global influences. As local cinema grows alongside the expansion of the media industry and an evolving national identity, filmmakers must navigate the tension between international commercial success, creative freedom, and staying true to home.


In this session, Professor Lim Song Hwee breaks down the rising phenomenon of Singapore-Taiwan co-productions to reveal how overseas funding, talent, and distribution are quietly reshaping local cinema. Following the presentation, he will be joined by a panel of film industry insiders to dive into the state of Singapore cinema, the reality of making movies today, and what truly gives a film its local soul.


—


Moderated by: Sim Jiaying, SGIFF Film Programmer and Lecturer

Sim Jiaying is a Lecturer at the University of Hong Kong and founder of the Singapore Film Database, a comprehensive digital resource on Singapore’s film ecosystem. She holds a PhD in Film and Television Studies from the University of Glasgow, with research focusing on Asian cinema, transnational screen cultures, and creative-critical practice. Her writing has appeared in Jom, Film-Philosophy, Journal of Chinese Cinemas, and anthologies by Edinburgh University Press and Routledge. She was a 2025 Hyundai Artlab Editorial Fellow. She has been working as a film programmer with SGIFF since 2024.

films.name: The Unknown
films.short_description: A reclusive Paris photographer follows a woman home from a party and wakes up the next morning inside her body, setting off an unnerving search for her identity and what he has become.
films.description:
David Zimmerman, a reclusive photographer who documents the changing edges of Paris, becomes fixated on a woman he meets at a party and follows her home. He wakes the next day inside her body and panic leads him into an investigation about her identity, coupled with the unsettling work of inhabiting a body, a self and a life that are not his. The swap is less a puzzle to solve than a kind of permanent homelessness, memories and desires contained in a body that no longer fits.


Arthur Harari's third feature is a psychological thriller that moves adroitly between realist Paris chronicle, investigation, melodrama and dream. Anchoring the film is Léa Seydoux’s masterful performance built on physical unease, playing a man’s mind trapped in another body.

Tsubasa and Gyotaro meet as boys in a small Japanese town and become inseparable as each other’s closest friend and foil, convinced the other understands him in a way no one else does. As they grow older, small misunderstandings pile up unspoken between them, leading to a quiet betrayal that forever ruptures their relationship. By the time their lives fork in adulthood, each man is carrying something the other never fully sees.

The film traces their parallel, mirrored paths, and the ache of realising—only in hindsight—the depth of a shared connection in spite of how different their lives turn out.

films.description:
Eight-year-old Josephine witnesses a violent crime at the park one morning while separated from her father. As her parents shield her from the reality of what happened, she tries to make sense of the event in her own way. Based on events in the director’s life, the film portrays a child’s fractured sense of safety and loss of innocence as she copes with trauma that is left unprocessed.


The evocative cinematography and sensitive writing bring to life a child’s psyche in all its complexities, while highlighting the parents’ interiorities with their own coping mechanisms. Directed with care and restraint, Josephine is a harrowing child’s-eye study of trauma amid the challenges of parenting in a world where violence could strike anytime.

films.short_description: Toll operators and lovers Santosh and Rajji spend their days waiting and working in decrepit booths. A tragic accident upturns their quiet lives in this magical realist love story of grief and acceptance.
films.description:
Rajji and Santosh are toll booth operators in the North Indian town of Nagina. The lovers spend slow days in decrepit booths accompanied by a science TV channel while dreaming of a better future. Just as their job demands them to be on the move often, the infrastructure around them sees continual transformation. When a sudden tragedy spawns a beguiling resurrection, the lives of Rajji and Santosh are also irreversibly changed.


Drawing from his experiences growing up in the upper Himalayas where the supernatural exists comfortably within the realm of reality, Yashasvi Juyal presents a magical realist love story that gently unfolds in layers of time and space, anchored by profound feelings of grief.

events.name: In Conversation With Anthony Wong
events.description:
Join the conversation with Hong Kong veteran Anthony Wong Chau-sang, who has over 150 acting credits since beginning his acting career with My Name Ain't Suzie in 1985. A familiar face in Hong Kong cinema, his acting credits include The Untold Story (1993), Beast Cops (1998), the Infernal Affairs trilogy (2002–2003) and Still Human (2018).


Renowned for his accomplished and versatile performances, he is the first Hong Kong actor to have won Best Actor awards in film, television and theatre. His honours include multiple Best Actor and Best Supporting Actor awards at the Hong Kong Film Awards, the Hong Kong Film Critics Society Awards, the Golden Bauhinia Awards, and the Golden Horse Awards.


In this exclusive dialogue session, Wong will share more about his illustrious four-decade long acting career, his creative pursuits across different mediums, and how he continues to thrive in an evolving global entertainment industry.

films.name: The Burning Giants
films.short_description: Along the Thai-Myanmar border, a mysterious illness marks Karen bodies with burns and an activist is killed for defending his village’s land, all while a toxic haze spreads across Western Thailand.
films.description:
A Karen man is picked up by forestry officers, his body marked by strange burns no doctor can explain, and taken to a quarantine facility. Elsewhere, drawing on a real-life killing, an Indigenous rights activist is chased from his village and dies for opposing its forced eviction. As a toxic haze creeps towards Thailand’s migrant workers, these separate lives are gradually revealed to be intertwined.


The Burning Giants unfolds without a single protagonist to anchor our gaze. Through measured cinematography, the film builds an immersive and atmospheric world with a magical realist register. The haunting sound design evokes the dread and grief that the images leave unsaid, allowing maladies, otherness and displacement to emerge from the smog with pointed social urgency.

films.description:
Kabul, 2021. Naru is the only female camera operator at the capital’s biggest television station. Separated from her husband, she raises her young son alone and is determined to live independently in a society where women’s choices remain closely controlled. Her career and personal life take a turn when she is assigned to work with Qodrat, a well-known journalist. Though initially dismissive, he gradually becomes fond of her.


Naru and Qodrat’s story unfolds alongside a city mired in violence and uncertainty as the US prepares to withdraw and the Taliban closes in. With naturalistic performances and a lively, grounded visual style, the film blends romance, humour and social observation, portraying a changing Afghanistan through Naru’s everyday life.

events.name: [Visionary Encounters] In-Depth Understanding: Asian Audience Behaviour
events.description:
It has never been more complicated for filmmakers and distributors to bring Southeast Asia audiences into cinemas. Hollywood tropes and stars are seen as tired. While local production has scaled up, other Asian content (Japanese anime, Korean blockbusters) can do well, competition for eyeballs

and consumer time is fierce, meaning that the theatrical experience is only one of many options open to consumers. With one of the most experienced film distribution and exhibition executives in our region, this session will examine the fast-evolving behaviour of consumers in SE Asia, why a giant studio like Warner Bros Discovery is getting into local production, and provide some tips on ‘audience design’.


Speaker

Kurt Rieder, Senior Vice President of Theatrical at Warner Bros Discovery APAC


Moderator

Patrick Frater, SGIFF Industry Specialist
events.short_description: Rare opportunity to understand what makes Southeast Asian audiences put aside their phones and spend two hours in a cinema.

films.short_description: A modest father in 1980s New York and his unremarkable family find their lives upturned by a get-rich scheme gone wrong. This textured crime thriller is anchored in performances that underscore the grandness, despair and humanity of wanting more.
films.description:
The Pearls, an unremarkable family in a 1980s New York suburb, live cordially, though sometimes anxious about money. Unlike his headstrong wife, Irwin is lamblike and easily swayed—especially when his flashy brother Gary comes knocking with a lucrative business idea. When the brothers’ eagerness to make bank ensnares all of them in a murky Russian group, the true price of their aspirations becomes clear.


James Gray, a longtime chronicler of retro America, serves up a crime thriller but tempers the genre’s excesses for an elegant human scale. With its celluloid textures and heavyweight performances, where strains in a voice feel like a cocked gun, Paper Tiger is a tactile exploration of the American Dream in its brilliant, brutal twilight.

In the late 1950s, bars and brothels flourish in the Wan Chai district of Hong Kong, catering to American and British soldiers on leave. When the madame of Lucky Bar arrives to scout for new girls from her fishing village, Shui Mei jumps at this coveted opportunity. Through the decades of a changing Hong Kong, Shui Mei’s vivacious spirit and entrepreneurial mindset tide her through the physical hardship and loneliness of her occupation.

films.description:
Halime is the only female competitive shooter in a Turkish village where the main trade is gunmaking. Inspired by her passion and achievements, her friends also begin to take an interest in shooting, but must seek their husbands’ permission to do so. When the local men’s shooting contest is cancelled, they successfully campaign to host a women’s shooting match, only to be confined to 32 metres of a shooting range instead of the usual 52 metres.


32 Meters depicts women’s continued struggle for parity in society and for their right to enjoy a life outside caregiving. It captures their joy when gathering with friends in pursuit of a hobby traditionally denied them—a simple act that proves empowering in a highly patriarchal society.

films.short_description: Caught between her separated parents in 1990s Singapore, a curious seven-year-old is left to carry big emotions she has no language for. How much children see, and how little they can do, slowly comes into focus.
films.description:
Seven-year-old Swee Swee insists on being called by her Chinese name, sells contraband chewing gum to her schoolmates and loudly pines for a boy in her class in 1994 Singapore. As her parents’ marriage dissolves, she and her sister are shuttled between a mother worn down by work and a father unwilling to show up. The sisters find in each other a rare steadiness that proves children’s innate capacity for care and love—even taking on the problems of adults.


Shot at a child's eye level, in a 4:3 frame limited in perspective yet capacious in feelings, the film gives shape to a child's overlooked emotional landscapes. Ah Girl asks what happens when adults are not intentional about parenthood and fail to see the child in front of them.

But tragedy soon strikes: Alice’s leg is nearly bitten off by a dog. To prevent her daughter from becoming a cripple, Anna strikes a deal with a mysterious woman, setting in motion a chain of deadly consequences. Twenty years later, Anna decides to tell her daughter the truth.


The Spiral is a morality thriller by one of Italy’s most promising horror filmmakers. In this Faustian tale, a woman’s ego and love for her children propel her into a whirlwind of bourgeois anxieties and entropy, powered by the inescapability of fate.

films.name: Local Sensations
films.description: Weaving glassblowing, nature walks, and a mock guide to monument design, Local Sensations is a dark satire on Thai society’s compulsion to sanctify everything it fears to question.

films.name: RIP ME, LOL
films.description: After a leaked sex tape drives her to suicide, Megan returns as a vengeful ghost haunting the men who wronged her.

films.name: The Bovine Comedy
films.description: In 2036, cows are nearly extinct. Phop owns Southeast Asia's last bull, but it is getting old. He employs Jon, the only person who can extract semen from it, and finds himself drawn to Jon’s hands.

films.name: Through the Cracks
films.description: Plagued by a persistent rattling noise inside his head, a soon-to-be bridegroom desperately searches for its source and discovers an irrepressible truth.

films.name: 9 Temples to Heaven
films.short_description: Faced with the imminent death of his mother, a man leads three generations of his family on a single-day temple pilgrimage—where prayer meets doubt, and reason wrestles with superstition.
films.description:
When a middle-aged businessman learns that his mother’s death is imminent, he packs the entire family of nine into a van for a single-day pilgrimage to nine temples, hoping to gain enough merit to alter her fate. But the road trip soon becomes fraught: old wounds resurface, alongside generational tension, marital strife, and clashing views on faith and modernity. As the matriarch begins to tire, the family reckon with their fractures and the reality of aging.


Drifting effortlessly between scientific rationality, spiritual recourse and the inevitability of mortality, the camera moves like a floating consciousness through architecture and landscapes. What emerges is a restrained commentary on Buddhist culture while the search for rationality crumbles.

events.name: PanelStory, or How a Housing Development is Born
events.description: This screening includes an online Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: PanelStory, or How a Housing Development is Born
films.short_description: A curious old man weaves his way through a labyrinthine housing estate. Through a dizzying exploration of neighbourly happenings in a public housing complex near Prague, the film forms an allegory for the complex dynamics of community-building.
films.description:
A mosaic of characters inhabit the gritty buildings in a Prague housing development. The flats are half-completed with poor plumbing and shoddy walls, while construction debris litter the unfinished estate. An elderly newcomer arrives from the countryside to move in with his daughter’s family; he roams the unmarked blocks to find the right building, chatting with strangers along the way. A young woman nearby discovers her friend’s home life is less enviable than it looks, and a boy slips out of kindergarten hoping to meet his father. Amid the chaos, residents improvise their own domestic lives.


Chytilová’s handheld camera captured the image of a community whose members pursue only their individual goals instead of shared socialist ideals. Small acts of kindness peek through undulating crises, all while the promise of a finished home looms.

films.name: Possible Love
films.short_description: A working-class family and a wealthy couple become entangled as they make a documentary together. Tensions simmer and loyalties shift in Lee Chang-dong’s exquisite, slow-burn drama, which asks if the distance between people can ever be closed.
films.description:
Blue-collar worker Ho-seok is left broken by a wave of layoffs and a violently repressed strike. He refuses therapy, while his wife Mi-ok holds down a factory job and keeps their family together. They become subjects of a documentary when Mi-ok befriends filmmaker Ye-ji, who senses dramatic potential in their pain. Backed by her rich husband, Ye-ji insinuates herself and her camera into their lives.


As the working class and the wealthy cross paths, desire and envy, fascination and appropriation shade into one another. Anchored by a stellar cast, this finely observed drama examines the fragile ideal of solidarity and the fraught quest for intimacy, asking if the distance between any two individuals can ever be closed.

films.description: Alone and isolated in a remote region of Indonesia during the early 1960s, a female Permesta fighter performs military drills and prepares for a Minahasan ancestral ritual.

films.name: Shadows
films.description: What begins as rehearsal becomes revelation when two young women discover that performance can reveal truths the script never intended.

films.name: She Said
films.description: On the day she is proposed to, a woman recounts her past in a scam compound. The vulnerability of her story blurs the line between memory, truth and reality.

films.name: Tropenkolder
films.description: Weary railway workers resist colonial labour through intentional slowness and refusal. As they disrupt a system built on constant movement, idleness becomes a subtle act of sabotage.

films.name: What Do You Seek in the Dark?
films.description: Loneliness draws a young man to a derelict cinema that was once a haunt for cruising men. Seeking release, he finds the cinema awakening, watching and luring him with an insisting gaze.

events.name: No Good Men
events.description: This screening includes a Q&A session with the filmmakers.

films.name: No Good Men
films.short_description: In Kabul on the eve of the Taliban’s return, a tenacious camerawoman’s career, relationships, family and freedom are thrown into uncertainty. She must decide what is worth holding on to and what she has to leave behind.
films.description:
Kabul, 2021. Naru is the only female camera operator at the capital’s biggest television station. Separated from her husband, she raises her young son alone and is determined to live independently in a society where women’s choices remain closely controlled. Her career and personal life take a turn when she is assigned to work with Qodrat, a well-known journalist. Though initially dismissive, he gradually becomes fond of her.


Naru and Qodrat’s story unfolds alongside a city mired in violence and uncertainty as the US prepares to withdraw and the Taliban closes in. With naturalistic performances and a lively, grounded visual style, the film blends romance, humour and social observation, portraying a changing Afghanistan through Naru’s everyday life.

films.name: Josephine
films.short_description: After eight-year-old Josephine witnesses a violent crime, the trauma lingers in profound ways as her parents try to shield her from adult realities.
films.description:
Eight-year-old Josephine witnesses a violent crime at the park one morning while separated from her father. As her parents shield her from the reality of what happened, she tries to make sense of the event in her own way. Based on events in the director’s life, the film portrays a child’s fractured sense of safety and loss of innocence as she copes with trauma that is left unprocessed.


The evocative cinematography and sensitive writing bring to life a child’s psyche in all its complexities, while highlighting the parents’ interiorities with their own coping mechanisms. Directed with care and restraint, Josephine is a harrowing child’s-eye study of trauma amid the challenges of parenting in a world where violence could strike anytime.

films.name: The Invisibles
films.short_description: Misadventures ensue as a protective single father and his three daughters—the youngest of whom is invisible—venture from their secluded life on a quiet island to Tokyo to meet the girls’ estranged grandmother, a famous actress who has taken ill.
films.description:
Widower Manabu and his three daughters live an isolated life on a verdant island to protect the family’s secret: the youngest child, Hikari, was born invisible. Harbouring ambitions of filmmaking and acting careers, the spirited sisters shoot home movies inspired by their distant maternal grandmother who is famed for an iconic horror role.


The matriarch’s sudden hospitalisation in Tokyo brings the family on a road trip replete with nerve-wracking accidents, comic encounters and candid conversations—exposing the risks to Hikari’s safety as well as Manabu’s parental anxieties. The Invisibles is a heartwarming fantastical film that discusses identity and disability with sympathy for both its young protagonists and a father whose love is compounded by grief.

films.name: "Vaterland" or A Bule Named Yanto
films.description: Reuniting with his sister in Yogyakarta, Yanto, a German-Indonesian, or bule, finds that she belongs effortlessly there. As envy and dissonance surface, his journey becomes a bittersweet exploration of his mixed-raced identity.

films.name: A Gentle Breeze
films.description: Returning from his uncle’s funeral, a boy becomes curious about his parents and life at home in Bagan.

films.name: Ashes and Echoes
films.description: Three interlinked stories about societal expectations: a father preparing his young son for conscription, two soldiers sharing intimate moments in a forest, and the filmmaker’s parents speaking about his childhood.

films.name: Surface Tension
films.description: Young swimmer Bulet returns to her hometown to attend a cousin’s wedding. Overwhelmed by grief and heartbreak, she tries to keep her head above water.

films.name: The Fever
films.description: Returning home after years abroad, a man finds that the locals are now consumed by a desire to leave. As a feverish contagion of unnamed dread spreads among them, young people mysteriously vanish.

films.name: The Days Off
films.short_description: As the moon threatens to ‘eclipse’ animals and people around her, 12-year-old Bego meets REN__, an online friend who teaches her how to ‘shift’ into her desired reality.
films.description:
During a seemingly endless summer break, 12-year-old Bego reckons with an approaching solar eclipse and struggles to fit in at home and with other girls. Her only solace is REN__, an online friend who teaches her how to ‘shift’ into her desired reality through lucid dreaming. As the moon threatens to ‘eclipse’ the animals and people around her, drawing them into a supernatural trance, Bego turns to ‘shifting’ in order to escape her melancholia and fears.


With its languid fades, shadows and lo-fi artifacting, The Days Off is a love letter to a bygone internet that sheltered misfits and dreamers. It curdles nostalgia with an otherworldly uncanniness that takes us deep into its meditation on the desires inherent in escapism.

films.name: Macho Dancer
films.short_description: Pol moves from the countryside to Manila in hopes of earning more money in the flesh industry. Amid the city’s chaos, he learns about the harsh yet alluring male prostitution business.
films.description:
In Manila’s red-light district, Pol takes up work at a nightclub performing as a ‘macho dancer’ for a predominantly queer audience. Under the tutelage of seasoned performer Noel, Pol is introduced to a world of hustle and desire shaped by unwritten rules. He toes the fine line between performance and survival, soon discovering certain truths close to home.


Lino Brocka frames Manila’s underground economy through the people who pass through it—corrupt cops, needy clients and dancers. In this seedy underbelly where intimacy is commodified and the marginalised are cast aside, Brocka focuses on the warmth in camaraderie within bleak confines.

films.name: Minotaur
films.short_description: As Russia descends into war, an influential businessowner in a small town decides whose lives are disposable. His betrayals pile up, exposing the moral and political corruption that insulates the powerful while the world burns.
films.description:
As Russia descends into war, Gleb, an influential businessowner in a small town, is asked to draw up a list of able-bodied staff he can spare for the draft. Meanwhile, his marriage has gone stale, and he suspects his wife is having an affair. With personal and professional pressures mounting, Gleb takes dramatic steps to protect his interests.


Exiled director Andrey Zvyagintsev transposes Claude Chabrol’s La Femme Infidèle onto wartime Russia, turning the erotic thriller into an indictment of the ruling class. Austere, widescreen compositions lend a disquieting elegance to this moral reckoning, in which the rot of society begins at home and human sacrifice is cruelly exacted to feed continual violence.

films.name: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
films.short_description: The road to a queer woman’s sexual awakening is paved with geysers of blood and radical vulnerability, powered by fantasy and imagination. Guilty pleasures have never felt more seen in this healing, tonally surprising take on the slasher genre.
films.description:
Geeky queer filmmaker Kris is tasked with reviving the Camp Miasma slasher franchise, with the goal of rehabilitating its transphobic reputation. She ventures into a remote campground to meet with the reclusive and enchanting Billy, who played the ‘final girl’ in the original film, hoping to persuade her to take on a cameo. Over spliffs, fried chicken and supermarket snacks, the two women bond, culminating in an ecstatic sexual awakening.


With copious stylistic throwbacks to definitive ’80s and ’90s horror, Jane Schoenberg’s third feature is packed with flesh and fluids while remaining tonally surprising. It resolutely celebrates libidinal liberation by giving space to raucous fantasies and freeing pleasures from guilty prison.

films.name: Sleep No More
films.short_description: Two sisters attempt to uncover the truth of their mother’s death amid possessions and hauntings in a wig factory. Indonesian director Edwin’s foray into horror highlights the systematic exploitation of workers through grotesque means.
films.description:
After Putri and Ida’s mother dies mysteriously at her workplace, the sisters replace her at the wig factory to pay off debts. As exhausted workers pull endless shifts under the watchful eyes of their boss, a slew of hair-raising supernatural encounters unfold. While deaths and possessions mount, their brother Bona, who has a special ability to regenerate body parts, becomes embroiled in the factory happenings.


Sleep No More draws strongly from ’80s Indonesian horror with its analogue visual effects and comical absurdity, and uses an oppressive spatial design to channel a deep sense of unease. The director’s first foray into horror presents an entertaining yet searing social commentary on the true demon of our times—capitalism.

films.name: La Bola Negra
films.short_description: Across epochs—Republican Spain in 1932, the Civil War in 1937 and contemporary Madrid in 2017—three men navigate historical turmoil and repression, connected by love, loss and literature, in this sweeping work of queer cinema.
films.description:
In Republican Spain in 1932, a young man applies for membership at a local casino and is rejected. During the Civil War in 1937, a conscripted musician looks after a wounded prisoner and builds a friendship with him. In modern-day Spain in 2017, a historian learns of his grandfather’s death and receives an unexpected inheritance. 


In La Bola Negra, nearly a century of Spanish political history enfolds the lives of these young men whose desires to be seen and accepted are thwarted by society’s conservatism. Directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi take inspiration from Federico García Lorca’s unfinished text La bola negra and Alberto Conejero’s play La piedra oscura, mixing real-life and fictional characters in this sweeping work of queer cinema.

films.name: Julián
films.short_description: New kid on the block Julián spends the summer with his grandmother and discovers the magic of the ocean when he decides to dress up for the Coney Island Mermaid Parade.
films.description:
Seven-year-old Julián spends the summer with his no-nonsense Dominican American grandmother Carmela in New York City, where he is introduced to his Caribbean heritage and the bustling Brooklyn community. When his new friends invite him to join them at the Coney Island Mermaid Parade, Julián recruits Carmela to make him a mermaid costume. Though he eventually finds that not everyone believes in his dream to become a mermaid, Julián is determined to make waves with the help of a magical ocean spirit.


An adaptation of the award-winning picture book, Julián Is a Mermaid, the film is rendered in 2D-animation in marker and coloured pencil style with a zesty palette. With Julián, animation studio Cartoon Saloon adds yet another lovingly crafted animation to their acclaimed filmography of whimsical and meaningful stories.

films.name: Hanabi
films.short_description: Hanabi depicts the people, flora and fauna, and natural and urban landscapes affected by the invisible dangers of radioactivity. Intricate imagery, sound design, narration and text form a polyphonic narrative about the relationship between civilisation, change and catastrophe.
films.description:
Made over ten years, Hanabi is loosely based on writer’s Yoko Hayasuke’s Diary of a Radioactive Brain, about the aftereffects of the Fukushima nuclear fallout following the 2011 Tohoku earthquake in Japan. Shot on 16mm film, this hybrid work includes Ana Vaz’s correspondences, clandestine footage captured by a Japanese worker during decontamination operations, and archival material.


Conversations with residents and activists, as well as depictions of rural, urban and natural landscapes, create a picture of diverse living beings affected by the invisible dangers of radioactivity. The film’s images, music, sound design, narration and text are sometimes at variance, creating dissonances in its polyphonic narrative. Hanabi also plays with time scales: the seasonal passage of months, the decades after a catastrophe, and the eternity of nuclear contamination. At once devastating and tender, this film poses open-ended questions about the relationship between civilisation and entropy.

films.name: Compact Disc
films.short_description: A filmmaker meets with his friends who were imprisoned after the 2019–20 protests in Hong Kong to talk about their fragmented memories from those years. The audiovisual materials and devices they examine suggest the challenges of finding truth and resolution through documentation.
films.description:
A filmmaker meets with his friends who were imprisoned after the 2019–20 protests in Hong Kong to examine memories and artefacts from those years. Their conversations about the changes since then unfold over audiovisual material from different recording devices and playback media, including surveillance and body cameras, news imagery, and footage from Wong’s vintage camcorder.


The distortions and pixellations of these images not only suggest the challenges of establishing indexical truth through documentation, but also reflect the group’s unresolved attempts to address the past through fragmented retellings and oblique humour. The film speaks to strength in the solidarity of friendship and shared experiences in the face of an unsettled past and unknowable future.

films.name: Fruits of Despair
films.short_description: While making a documentary about the Israel-Palestine conflict, an Iranian filmmaker finds himself in a warzone when Israel and the US attack Iran in early 2026. This hybrid film connects displacement, loss and mortality that span decades across borders.
films.description:
While making a documentary inspired by archival footage about the longstanding conflict between Israel and Palestine, Nima Nassaj is plunged into a warzone himself when Israel and the US attack Iran in early 2026. As he evacuates Tehran with his family, his film transforms: present-day images and sounds of violence layer over those from the past. News clips, citizen phone footage, social media posts and Nassaj’s video diary capturing the strikes are interspersed with ruminations on displacement, disempowerment and mortality.


The hybrid film explores the personal and collective destruction wreaked by cross-border, decades-long conflicts. Pondering the deaths of Palestinian filmmakers like Hani Jawharieh, Nassaj understands that images must survive to tell these stories.

films.name: In Sum
films.short_description: Glitchy fragments shot by an obsolete digital camera overlay archival films about rural development in Thailand during the Cold War, presenting competing perspectives about national stability and regional security.
films.description:
Incorporating propaganda films from the 1960s and the socialist docudrama Tongpan (1977), In Sum examines the contested Cold War histories of rural northeastern Thailand through a metafilmic lens. The poor and remote region was considered at risk for communist insurgencies in the 1960s and ’70s, and became a site of unevenly administered agricultural and infrastructure projects in the name of national security.


Archival images are overlaid with distorted footage shot by an almost inoperable digital camera, recovered from Napattaloong’s old home, that seems to voice its exhaustion. The fractured imagery questions the assumptions behind geostrategic allegiances and national narratives of moderation and stability.

films.name: Filipiñana
films.short_description: In this stylish and darkly funny feature debut, a tee girl’s mission to return a golf club to the country club president leads her to uncover sinister secrets about her workplace, exposing elite society’s dark underbelly.
films.description:
Isabel is a newly hired tee girl at a posh resort on Manila’s outskirts. In between her duties on the driving range, the teenager roams the golf course reminiscent of her lush Ilocano homeland. Tasked to return a golf club to the country club’s charismatic president, Isabel wanders deeper into its insulated interior spaces, witnessing how labour and servitude are performed in careful choreography and deference to Chinese tourists and wealthy industrialists.


Her curiosity and growing boldness lead her to discover violent secrets lurking just behind the lavish facade. Rafael Manuel’s sun-drenched, stylish debut feature unfurls at a languid pace that belies its incisive exposé of elite society’s dark underbelly.

films.name: House of the Wind
films.short_description: An elderly woman builds a house to entice her children working in Europe to return to Cameroon, but a surprising companionship with a young woman in her neighbourhood upends all she believed about familial ties.
films.description:
Josette, 80, spends her days overseeing the construction of a house that is meant to entice her children working in Europe to move back to Cameroon. Things take a turn when Sarah, a young street vendor in her neighbourhood, asks her for a favour, to which she begrudgingly agrees. Personal boundaries begin to blur as Josette’s affection and concern for Sarah grow, for better and for worse.


House of the Wind follows Josette’s search for companionship, both found in and withheld by blood and chosen family. Unexpected beginnings and ends present unique challenges in this intimate and tender portrait of loneliness during one’s twilight years.

films.name: Brave Cat
films.short_description: A young forest cat embarks on a courageous journey to find her mother, joined by new friends also searching for lost family.
films.description:
Animals have been disappearing from the forest, kidnapped by the human—a giant monster who forces them to join his circus. Years after witnessing her mother’s abduction by the human’s guard dogs, Kona, a young cat, gathers the courage to search for her.


Traversing woodland and glaciers, venturing all the way out to sea, Kona embarks on a transformative journey accompanied by Colin, a puppy abandoned by the guard dogs due to his disability, and Bernard, a plucky big bear who repeatedly escapes from the circus. Chased by the guard dogs and faced with the challenge of navigating unfamiliar environments, they bond over their shared hope of reuniting with lost family.


In this uplifting adventure, friendship fosters the strength to stand together and put an end to terror. Filled with wonder and heart, Brave Cat is a richly textured work of animation that tells an empathetic story about loss and forgiveness, reflecting imaginatively upon the universal theme of human rights.

films.name: The Unknown
films.short_description: A reclusive Paris photographer follows a woman home from a party and wakes up the next morning inside her body, setting off an unnerving search for her identity and what he has become.
films.description:
David Zimmerman, a reclusive photographer who documents the changing edges of Paris, becomes fixated on a woman he meets at a party and follows her home. He wakes the next day inside her body and panic leads him into an investigation about her identity, coupled with the unsettling work of inhabiting a body, a self and a life that are not his. The swap is less a puzzle to solve than a kind of permanent homelessness, memories and desires contained in a body that no longer fits.


Arthur Harari's third feature is a psychological thriller that moves adroitly between realist Paris chronicle, investigation, melodrama and dream. Anchoring the film is Léa Seydoux’s masterful performance built on physical unease, playing a man’s mind trapped in another body.

events.name: Tangles

films.name: Tangles
films.short_description: A young graphic artist returns home to care for her mother who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer’s. In the process, she finds grief, comedy and first love tangled together in a household relearning how to love a person they thought they knew.
films.description:
Sarah puts her exciting life as an activist and artist in 90s San Francisco on hold and returns to her small, conservative hometown after her mother’s Alzheimer’s diagnosis. While her father struggles with his own grief, Sarah’s caregiving duty affects every part of her life, including her romantic relationship. Despite the heartrending effects of Alzheimer’s, the film imbues her mother with a personality beyond the disease: feisty, funny, with flashes of her old self.


Tangles adapts Sarah Leavitt’s memoir for the screen without sanding down its unique traits as a graphic novel. Hand-drawn, black-and-white animation reimagines the source visual language, using sound design and movement to give the story a life distinctly its own, staying faithful to both mediums.

films.name: Prosecution
films.short_description: Amid a rise in far-right extremism and racially motivated attacks, Seyo Kim, a young German-Korean state prosecutor, impartially executes the law. But when a masked individual attempts to set her on fire, her engagement with the law becomes personal.
films.description:
Seyo Kim, a promising state prosecutor, is determined to be an impartial representative of the state and sets aside her misgivings about the dismissal of charges for racist attacks. But when an encounter with far-right individuals in court results in an attack on her life, Seyo goes against orders and takes the investigation into her hands. Uncovering an extensive network of fascist extremists, she begins to question who the so-called neutrality of institutions really serves.


Prosecution confronts the rise in far-right extremism and the systemic failure of institutions in Germany to protect their most vulnerable citizens. As Seyo combines vigilantism with legal recourse, the film makes a case for extreme solutions to extremist violence.

films.name: Amores Perros
films.short_description: A fatal car crash links three strangers’ lives: a young man entering the world of dogfighting, a supermodel whose life is derailed after the accident, and an ex-guerrilla trying to reconcile with his past.
films.description:
The lives of three strangers from different segments of society intertwine after a tragic car crash in Mexico city: a young man who enters the feral world of dogfighting to make money in order to run away with his brother’s wife. A supermodel whose life has been derailed by the crash and is struggling to find her dog that has disappeared into her apartment floorboard. And an aging hitman who lives with a pack of stray dogs and is desperate to reconnect with his estranged daughter.


Iñárritu’s unflinching feature debut, like a rabid mongrel, latches onto these characters as they seek reprieve from their respective circumstances. Amid the messy cycles of violence in a relentlessly harsh city marked by segregation, they struggle to find human connection.

films.name: Everytime
films.short_description: In this intimate study of grief, a mother, daughter and teenage boy are drawn into the orbit of an absent loved one. They take a trip to a seaside resort, where reality shimmers under the glistening sun and time folds into itself.
films.description:
On the eve of a family holiday, teenager Jessie climbs onto a roof and ventures too close to the edge. A year later, her mother, sister and boyfriend try to live with a semblance of normalcy while still reeling from their devastating loss. Each struggles privately with blame and incomprehension, yet they remain bound together by the gaping hole in their hearts. The unlikely trio embark on the trip that never happened, arriving at a resort where memories of the past collide with the unbearable present.


Featuring adroit cinematography and layered performances, Everytime examines the effects of grief on perception: its strange power to bend time and suspend logic, if only briefly.

films.name: The End of It
films.short_description: Claire announces at her 250th birthday party her decision to die, which is challenged by family and friends. As her final day approaches, she turns her death into an artist’s statement.
films.description:
In the future, aging is no longer a problem and death is optional. Once an artist of great renown, Claire announces her wish to die at her 250th birthday celebration. Friends, as well as her husband and AI assistant, try to talk her out of it. But Claire is determined not only to finalise the logistics involved in her decision, but also to turn her final moments on earth into a profound and meaningful piece of performance art.


In this thought-provoking feature debut, Maria Martínez Bayona confronts this generation’s obsession with youth and beauty with an existential spectacle of what it means to be alive. The End of It is a darkly humorous tale of freedom featuring a stellar lead performance by Rebecca Hall.
